docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// business layer/metier.interface.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The business layer contract. The 11 methods of the JSON server (reading
// for lists, calendar, and adding/deleting an appointment), plus 2
// methods for the patient area and 6 methods for managing doctors
// and client management.
// =========================================================================

import { Client } from '../entities/client.entity';
import { Creneau } from '../entities/creneau.entity';
import { Medecin } from '../entities/medecin.entity';
import { Rv } from '../entities/rv.entity';
import { AgendaMedecinJour } from '../domain/agenda-medecin-jour';

// the data entered in the “doctor” or “client” form
export interface DonneesPersonne {
  titre: string; // Mr., Mrs., Ms.
  nom: string;
  prenom: string;
   // creation: optional; defaults to the name in lowercase
   // Modification: optional; the login remains unchanged if it is missing
  login?: string;
   // creation: optional; defaults to the username
   // update: optional; the password remains unchanged if omitted
  password?: string;
   // modification: the version of the record at the time the form was
   // displayed (optimistic lock, see AbstractEntity.version)
  version?: number;
}

export interface IMetier {
   // ------------------------------------------------ readings (unchanged)
  getAllClients(): Promise<Client[]>;
  getAllMedecins(): Promise<Medecin[]>;
  getAllCreneaux(idMedecin: number): Promise<Creneau[]>;
  getRvMedecinJour(idMedecin: number, jour: string): Promise<Rv[]>;
  getClientById(id: number): Promise<Client | null>;
  getMedecinById(id: number): Promise<Medecin | null>;
  getRvById(id: number): Promise<Rv | null>;
  getCreneauById(id: number): Promise<Creneau | null>;
  getAgendaMedecinJour(idMedecin: number, jour: string): Promise<AgendaMedecinJour | null>;
   /** the client (patient) whose user account is [idUser], or null */
  getClientByUserId(idUser: number): Promise<Client | null>;
   /** a client’s appointments, either today’s or future ones, with time slot and doctor */
  getRvAVenirClient(idClient: number): Promise<Rv[]>;

   // ------------------------------------------------ appointments (ADMIN, DOCTOR, USER)
  /**
   * lève une MetierException si :
   *  - le jour est passé ('ERRORS.PAST_DATE') ;
   *  - le patient a déjà un rendez-vous à venir ('ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT') ;
   *  - le créneau est déjà pris ce jour-là ('ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED').
   */
  ajouterRv(jour: string, creneau: Creneau, client: Client): Promise<Rv>;
  supprimerRv(rv: Rv): Promise<void>;

   // ------------------------------------------------ doctors (ADMIN)
   /** creates the doctor ET's user account (role DOCTOR) */
  ajouterMedecin(donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Medecin>;
   /** Modifies the physician ET’s user account */
  modifierMedecin(id: number, donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Medecin>;
   /** deletes the doctor, his time slots, and his account (ET) — rejected if he has appointments */
  supprimerMedecin(id: number): Promise<void>;

   // ------------------------------------------------ clients
   // (ADMIN; ajouterClient is also used to register a patient,
   // modifierClient and supprimerClient for the patient to create their own account)
   /** creates the client ET and their user account (role USER) */
  ajouterClient(donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Client>;
  modifierClient(id: number, donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Client>;
  /**
   * supprime le client, son compte ET tous ses rendez-vous (passés et futurs).
   * Utilisée par l'ADMIN (page "Clients") et par le patient lui-même
   * ("Gérer mon compte").
   */
  supprimerClient(id: number): Promise<void>;
}

export const METIER_TOKEN = 'IMetier';
  • lines 17–30: the data for a doctor or client to be created or modified. Username and password are optional: upon creation, they default to the name in lowercase; upon modification, they change only if they have been entered;
  • lines 32–78: the business layer contract—what other layers can request from it. The comments [/** ... */] are documentation comments, displayed by [VS Code] when you hover over the method;
  • line 80: the token under which the implementation is registered in [app.module.ts]. A [TypeScript] interface disappears at compile time: it cannot be used for dependency injection. Therefore, injection is performed using this token: [@Inject(METIER_TOKEN)].

docs.title: 11.11.4. src/metier/metier.service.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// business/metier.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Implementation of the business layer.
//
// The readings and calendar are taken as-is from the server JSON. The
// new feature is the management of doctors and clients, which follows three
// management rules:
//
//    1. A person (doctor or client) and their user account are
//       TOUJOURS together: they are created, modified, and deleted together, within
//       a single TRANSACTION—either everything succeeds, or nothing is written;
//    2. The login is unique throughout the application, and two doctors (or
//       two customers) cannot have the same first and last names;
//    3. Deletion:
//       - A MÉDECIN with appointments cannot be deleted (its
//         patients would lose their appointments without being notified): you must
//         cancel them first. Its time slots disappear along with it;
//       - a CLIENT, on the other hand, disappears along with TOUS its appointments (past and
//         future) — regardless of whether the deletion is initiated by the ADMIN or the patient
//         .
//
// And two rules for scheduling appointments, regardless of the role of
// the person making the reservation (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient themselves):
//    4. No appointments in the past;
//    5. A patient may have only one upcoming appointment at a time.
//
// Doctors and patients follow exactly the same rules: the common code
// is written UNE times (private methods xxxPersonne), and configured by a
// small “descriptor” that indicates what type of person we’re dealing with.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { DataSource, EntityManager, QueryFailedError } from 'typeorm';
import * as bcrypt from 'bcryptjs';
import { DonneesPersonne, IMetier } from './metier.interface';
import { MetierException } from './metier.exception';
import { MedecinRepository } from '../repositories/medecin.repository';
import { ClientRepository } from '../repositories/client.repository';
import { CreneauRepository } from '../repositories/creneau.repository';
import { RvRepository } from '../repositories/rv.repository';
import { UserRepository } from '../repositories/user.repository';
import { Client } from '../entities/client.entity';
import { Creneau } from '../entities/creneau.entity';
import { Medecin } from '../entities/medecin.entity';
import { Personne } from '../entities/personne.entity';
import { Rv } from '../entities/rv.entity';
import { Role, User } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { AgendaMedecinJour } from '../domain/agenda-medecin-jour';
import { CreneauMedecinJour } from '../domain/creneau-medecin-jour';
import { aujourdhui } from './dates';

// number of bcrypt salt rounds—the same as in the SQL script ($2b$10$...)
const TOURS_BCRYPT = 10;

// what the two DAO MedecinRepository and ClientRepository have in common
// (TypeScript checks the compatibility of objects via FORME: both
// classes implement this interface without having to declare it)
interface PersonneDao<T extends Personne> {
  findById(id: number, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<T | null>;
  findByPrenomNom(prenom: string, nom: string, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<T | null>;
  save(personne: T, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<T>;
  deleteById(id: number, manager?: EntityManager): Promise<void>;
}

// everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client in terms of business rules
interface DescripteurPersonne<T extends Personne> {
  dao: PersonneDao<T>;
  fabriquer: () => T; // new Doctor() or new Client()
  role: Role; // DOCTOR or USER
  cleIntrouvable: string; // message if the person does not exist
  cleExisteDeja: string; // message if the same first and last names already exist
   // optional: if present, deletion is REFUSÉE as long as the person
   // has appointments (compterRv > 0), with the message cleAvecRv
  compterRv?: (id: number, manager: EntityManager) => Promise<number>;
  cleAvecRv?: string;
   // optional: what to delete for the person (the rows that
   // refer to them via a foreign key)
  avantSuppression?: (id: number, manager: EntityManager) => Promise<void>;
}

@Injectable()
export class MetierService implements IMetier {
  private readonly medecinDescripteur: DescripteurPersonne<Medecin>;
  private readonly clientDescripteur: DescripteurPersonne<Client>;

  constructor(
     // DataSource: the connection TypeORM itself, provided by
     // TypeOrmModule.forRoot(...). It is not used QUE to open
     // transactions (dataSource.transaction(...))—the requests, on the other hand,
     // remain in the DAO layer.
    private readonly dataSource: DataSource,
    private readonly medecinRepository: MedecinRepository,
    private readonly clientRepository: ClientRepository,
    private readonly creneauRepository: CreneauRepository,
    private readonly rvRepository: RvRepository,
    private readonly userRepository: UserRepository,
  ) {
    this.medecinDescripteur = {
      dao: medecinRepository,
      fabriquer: () => new Medecin(),
      role: 'DOCTOR',
      cleIntrouvable: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND',
      cleExisteDeja: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
      compterRv: (id, manager) => rvRepository.countByMedecin(id, manager),
      cleAvecRv: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS',
       // A walk-in doctor may still have available time slots:
       // they no longer make sense without it, so they are deleted along with it (otherwise
       // the foreign key creneaux.id_medecin would prevent the deletion).
      avantSuppression: (id, manager) => creneauRepository.deleteByMedecin(id, manager),
    };
    this.clientDescripteur = {
      dao: clientRepository,
      fabriquer: () => new Client(),
      role: 'USER',
      cleIntrouvable: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND',
      cleExisteDeja: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
       // no compterRv: deleting a client is never denied;
       // their appointments (past and future) are deleted along with them (otherwise
       // the foreign key rv.id_client would prevent deletion)
      avantSuppression: (id, manager) => rvRepository.deleteByClient(id, manager),
    };
  }

  // =======================================================================
   // read operations—unchanged compared to the server JSON
  // =======================================================================

  getAllClients(): Promise<Client[]> {
    return this.clientRepository.findAll();
  }

  getAllMedecins(): Promise<Medecin[]> {
    return this.medecinRepository.findAll();
  }

  getAllCreneaux(idMedecin: number): Promise<Creneau[]> {
    return this.creneauRepository.getAllCreneaux(idMedecin);
  }

  getRvMedecinJour(idMedecin: number, jour: string): Promise<Rv[]> {
    return this.rvRepository.getRvMedecinJour(idMedecin, jour);
  }

  getClientById(id: number): Promise<Client | null> {
    return this.clientRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getMedecinById(id: number): Promise<Medecin | null> {
    return this.medecinRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getRvById(id: number): Promise<Rv | null> {
    return this.rvRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getCreneauById(id: number): Promise<Creneau | null> {
    return this.creneauRepository.findById(id);
  }

  getClientByUserId(idUser: number): Promise<Client | null> {
    return this.clientRepository.findByUserId(idUser);
  }

  getRvAVenirClient(idClient: number): Promise<Rv[]> {
    return this.rvRepository.findAVenirByClient(idClient, aujourdhui());
  }

   // same algorithm as the server JSON (and as the original Spring project)
  async getAgendaMedecinJour(idMedecin: number, jour: string): Promise<AgendaMedecinJour | null> {
    const medecin = await this.getMedecinById(idMedecin);
    if (medecin === null) {
      return null;
    }
    const creneauxHoraires = await this.getAllCreneaux(idMedecin);
    const reservations = await this.getRvMedecinJour(idMedecin, jour);
    const hReservations = new Map<number, Rv>();
    for (const resa of reservations) {
      hReservations.set(resa.idCreneau, resa);
    }
    const creneauxMedecinJour = creneauxHoraires.map(
      (creneau) => new CreneauMedecinJour(creneau, hReservations.get(creneau.id) ?? null),
    );
    return new AgendaMedecinJour(medecin, jour, creneauxMedecinJour);
  }

  // =======================================================================
   // appointment
  // =======================================================================

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
   // scheduling an appointment, within a transaction:
   /  / 1. no past appointments;
   /  / 2. on the patient’s line (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE): if the
   /     / same patient books two time slots at the same time (two tabs,
   /     / double-click...), the second transaction waits for the
   /     / first one—and then sees the appointment it just created;
   /  / 3. only one upcoming appointment per patient;
   /  / 4. Finally, the insertion. If the time slot has just been booked by a AUTRE
   /     / patient, it is the constraint SQL unq1_rv (day, id_creneau) that
   /     / prevents insertion—translated to MetierException by transaction().
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  ajouterRv(jour: string, creneau: Creneau, client: Client): Promise<Rv> {
    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      const aujourd = aujourdhui();
      if (jour < aujourd) {
        throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PAST_DATE');
      }
      if ((await this.clientRepository.verrouiller(client.id, manager)) === null) {
        throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND');
      }
      if ((await this.rvRepository.countAVenirByClient(client.id, aujourd, manager)) > 0) {
        throw new MetierException('ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT');
      }
      const rv = new Rv();
      rv.jour = jour;
      rv.creneau = creneau;
      rv.client = client;
      return this.rvRepository.save(rv, manager);
    });
  }

  async supprimerRv(rv: Rv): Promise<void> {
    await this.rvRepository.deleteById(rv.id);
  }

  // =======================================================================
   // doctors and clients—public methods delegate to
   // shared private methods, with the correct descriptor
  // =======================================================================

  ajouterMedecin(donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Medecin> {
    return this.ajouterPersonne(this.medecinDescripteur, donnees);
  }

  modifierMedecin(id: number, donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Medecin> {
    return this.modifierPersonne(this.medecinDescripteur, id, donnees);
  }

  supprimerMedecin(id: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.supprimerPersonne(this.medecinDescripteur, id);
  }

  ajouterClient(donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Client> {
    return this.ajouterPersonne(this.clientDescripteur, donnees);
  }

  modifierClient(id: number, donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Client> {
    return this.modifierPersonne(this.clientDescripteur, id, donnees);
  }

   // the client, their account ET all their appointments (ADMIN, or the patient
   // themselves via “Manage My Account”: same method, same rule)
  supprimerClient(id: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.supprimerPersonne(this.clientDescripteur, id);
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
   // creation: the user account first (the person references it),
   // then the person—all within the UNE transaction.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private ajouterPersonne<T extends Personne>(d: DescripteurPersonne<T>, donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<T> {
    const nom = donnees.nom.trim().toUpperCase();
    const prenom = donnees.prenom.trim();
     // Rules for the dbrdvmedecins2 database: login = name in lowercase,
     // password = login—unless the user has entered others
    const login = (donnees.login || nom).toLowerCase();
    const password = donnees.password || login;

    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      await this.verifierPersonneUnique(d, prenom, nom, null, manager);
      await this.verifierLoginLibre(login, manager);

      const user = new User();
      user.login = login;
      user.password = await bcrypt.hash(password, TOURS_BCRYPT);
      user.nom = `${prenom} ${nom}`;
      user.role = d.role;
      await this.userRepository.save(user, manager);

      const personne = d.fabriquer();
      personne.titre = donnees.titre;
      personne.nom = nom;
      personne.prenom = prenom;
      personne.user = user;
      return d.dao.save(personne, manager);
    });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
   // Change: the user ET must update their account (the displayed name "first name NOM"
   // must follow; the login and password only change if they have been
   // entered).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private modifierPersonne<T extends Personne>(
    d: DescripteurPersonne<T>,
    id: number,
    donnees: DonneesPersonne,
  ): Promise<T> {
    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      const personne = await d.dao.findById(id, manager);
      if (personne === null) {
        throw new MetierException(d.cleIntrouvable);
      }
       // optimistic lock: if the version in the database is no longer the same as the
       // form, someone has modified this record in the meantime—the system refuses
       // rather than silently overwriting their changes.
      if (donnees.version !== undefined && donnees.version !== personne.version) {
        throw new MetierException('ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE');
      }

      personne.titre = donnees.titre;
      personne.nom = donnees.nom.trim().toUpperCase();
      personne.prenom = donnees.prenom.trim();
      await this.verifierPersonneUnique(d, personne.prenom, personne.nom, id, manager);

      const user = personne.user;
      user.nom = `${personne.prenom} ${personne.nom}`;
      if (donnees.login && donnees.login.toLowerCase() !== user.login) {
        const login = donnees.login.toLowerCase();
        await this.verifierLoginLibre(login, manager);
        user.login = login;
      }
      if (donnees.password) {
        user.password = await bcrypt.hash(donnees.password, TOURS_BCRYPT);
      }
      await this.userRepository.save(user, manager);
      return d.dao.save(personne, manager);
    });
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
   // deletion, in UNE transaction, in the order dictated by the foreign keys
   //:
   /  / 1. Possible refusal if there are still available appointments (with a doctor);
   /  / 2. Information identifying the person (a doctor’s time slots, a client’s
   /     / for a client);
   /  / 3. the person (who references their account);
   /  / 4. their account.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private supprimerPersonne<T extends Personne>(d: DescripteurPersonne<T>, id: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.transaction(async (manager) => {
      const personne = await d.dao.findById(id, manager);
      if (personne === null) {
        throw new MetierException(d.cleIntrouvable);
      }
      if (d.compterRv && (await d.compterRv(id, manager)) > 0) {
        throw new MetierException(d.cleAvecRv ?? 'ERRORS.INVALID_FORM');
      }
      if (d.avantSuppression) {
        await d.avantSuppression(id, manager);
      }
      await d.dao.deleteById(id, manager);
      await this.userRepository.deleteById(personne.idUser, manager);
    });
  }

   // Rejects first and last names already used by a AUTRE person of the same type
   // (idCourant: the person being edited, who obviously has the
   // right to keep their own first and last names; null for a new creation)
  private async verifierPersonneUnique<T extends Personne>(
    d: DescripteurPersonne<T>,
    prenom: string,
    nom: string,
    idCourant: number | null,
    manager: EntityManager,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const homonyme = await d.dao.findByPrenomNom(prenom, nom, manager);
    if (homonyme !== null && homonyme.id !== idCourant) {
      throw new MetierException(d.cleExisteDeja);
    }
  }

  private async verifierLoginLibre(login: string, manager: EntityManager): Promise<void> {
    if ((await this.userRepository.findByLogin(login, manager)) !== null) {
      throw new MetierException('ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN');
    }
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
   // executes [travail] in a transaction: dataSource.transaction() performs
   // START TRANSACTION, calls [travail] with a EntityManager linked to this
   // transaction, then COMMIT if everything went well—or ROLLBACK if an
   // exception was thrown (including MetierException).
  //
   // The "free login" and "unique first name + last name" checks are performed AVANT
   // during the write operation, to provide a clear message. However, two ADMIN entries could
   // register the same login (or the same doctor) at the same time: in this
   // rare case, a uniqueness constraint SQL rejects the second
   // write—we then map this error SQL to the same MetierException.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  private async transaction<R>(travail: (manager: EntityManager) => Promise<R>): Promise<R> {
    try {
      return await this.dataSource.transaction(travail);
    } catch (e) {
      throw traduireDoublon(e);
    }
  }
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Uniqueness constraint violations -> MetierException
//
// When a constraint UNIQUE rejects a write operation, MySQL returns the error
// ER_DUP_ENTRY (No. 1062), whose message cites the constraint’s NOM:
//    Duplicate entry 'marie-pelissier' for key 'medecins.unq_medecins_prenom_nom'
// (MySQL prefixes the name with the table name, MariaDB does not). This is why
// this reason that the script SQL NOMME all of its constraints: each can then
// be translated into its own message.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
const MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES: Record<string, string> = {
  unq_users_login: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN',
  unq_medecins_prenom_nom: 'ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS',
  unq_clients_prenom_nom: 'ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS',
  unq1_rv: 'ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED',
};

// returns the MetierException corresponding to the violated constraint, or
// the original error, unchanged, if it is not a known violation
function traduireDoublon(e: unknown): unknown {
  if (!(e instanceof QueryFailedError)) {
    return e;
  }
  const erreurSql = e.driverError as { code?: string; sqlMessage?: string };
  if (erreurSql?.code !== 'ER_DUP_ENTRY') {
    return e;
  }
   // "... for key 'medecins.unq_medecins_prenom_nom'" -> "unq_medecins_prenom_nom"
  const contrainte = /for key '(?:[^'.]*\.)?([^']+)'/.exec(erreurSql.sqlMessage ?? e.message)?.[1];
  const cle = contrainte ? MESSAGES_CONTRAINTES[contrainte] : undefined;
  return cle ? new MetierException(cle) : e;
}

This is the most comprehensive file in the application. Let’s break it down section by section.

docs.title: 11.11.4.1. The descriptors
docs.text:
• line 54: the cost of bcrypt, the same as in the script SQL;
  • lines 59–64: what the DAO files for doctors and clients have in common. [TypeScript] compares types by their form: [MedecinRepository] and [ClientRepository] satisfy this interface without declaring it ([implements]);
  • Lines 67–80: Everything that distinguishes a doctor from a client in terms of business logic: its DAO, how to create an instance, the role of its account, its error messages, and what happens when it is deleted. Since doctors and clients follow the same rules, the code for these rules is written once, in generic methods parameterized by a descriptor;
  • lines 87–98: the constructor receives the [DataSource] (to open transactions) and the five DAO. It constructs the two descriptors. The one for doctors (lines 99–111) prevents the deletion of a doctor who has appointments ([compterRv]) and deletes their time slots before the doctor is deleted ([avantSuppression]). The one for clients (lines 112–122) does not have a [compterRv]: a client is deleted along with their appointments.

docs.title: 11.11.4.2. Read operations and the calendar
docs.text:
• lines 129–167: the queries delegate to the DAO layer;
  • lines 170–185: calendar calculation. The doctor’s time slots and today’s appointments are read; the appointments are stored in a [Map] indexed by their time slot ID; then each time slot is associated with its appointment, or with [null]. The [Map] avoids having to scan the list of appointments for each time slot.

docs.title: 11.11.4.3. Scheduling an appointment
docs.text:
• lines 203–221: everything takes place within a single transaction;
  • lines 206–208: no appointments in the past;
  • lines 209–211: the patient’s record is locked. Without this lock, two appointments for the same patient submitted at the same time (two tabs, a double-click) could both pass the following test before either one has written its appointment to the database. With the lock, the second transaction waits for the first to finish, then sees the appointment it created;
  • lines 212–214: only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  • lines 215–219: the insertion. If another patient has just booked the same time slot, the constraint [unq1_rv] rejects the insertion, and the method [transaction] handles the error (see below);
  • lines 223–225: deleting an appointment.

docs.title: 11.11.4.4. Management of Doctors and Clients
docs.text:
• lines 232–256: the six public methods delegate to the three generic methods, using the correct descriptor;
  • Lines 262–288: Creation. The name is capitalized; by default, the username is the name in lowercase, and the password is the username (lines 267–268). Within the transaction: uniqueness rules are verified, the account is created (the password is hashed), followed by the person, who is linked to the account. If the second write operation fails, the first is rolled back: an account is never created without a person;
  • lines 295–299: the update. The optimistic lock (lines 308–310) rejects a record that has been modified in the meantime. The displayed name of the account follows the first name and last name; the username and password change only if they have been entered;
  • lines 341–356: deletion, in the order dictated by foreign keys: possible rejection (a doctor who has appointments), deletion of references to the person (a doctor’s time slots, a client’s appointments), deletion of the person, then deletion of their account;
  • lines 361–367: a person with the same name is rejected, unless it is the person themselves (modification);
  • lines 374–378: a username that is already taken is rejected.

docs.title: 11.11.4.5. Transactions and Uniqueness Constraints
docs.text:
• lines 392–398: All entries go through this method: [dataSource.transaction] validates or cancels the transaction (see Example 28), and an error is represented by [traduireDoublon];
  • lines 411–416: each named uniqueness constraint in the SQL script has its own error message;
  • lines 420–432: an error SQL ([QueryFailedError]) with code [ER_DUP_ENTRY] is a uniqueness constraint violation. Its message includes the constraint name (prefixed by the table name with [MySQL] 8, without a prefix with [MariaDB]): the regular expression on line 429 extracts it. A known constraint becomes [MetierException]; any other error is reported as-is: this is a genuine anomaly.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.constants.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Where does the token JWT go?
//
// With the Angular client, it was the client’s code `JavaScript` that stored
// the token (localStorage) and added it to every request itself (header
// "Authorization: Bearer ..."). A browser that displays ordinary HTML
// does not know how to do this: for it to include the token
// on its own with every request, it must be stored in a COOKIE.
//
// The settings for this cookie are important for security:
//    - httpOnly: the page’s JavaScript cannot read the cookie (an
//      injected script would therefore not be able to steal the token);
//    - sameSite 'lax': the browser does not send PAS the cookie with a POST
//      from another site. Since all actions that modify
//      data are POST, a page embedded on another site cannot
//      reserve or delete anything by impersonating
//      the user (a so-called CSRF attack);
//    - secure: in production (HTTPS), the cookie is never transmitted in plain text;
//    - maxAge: the cookie disappears when the token expires.
// =========================================================================

import { CookieOptions } from 'express';

export const COOKIE_JWT = 'rdvmedecins_jwt';

export const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET ?? 'dev-secret-a-changer-en-production';

export const JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS = process.env.JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS
  ? parseInt(process.env.JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS, 10)
  : 7200;

export function optionsCookieJwt(): CookieOptions {
  return {
    httpOnly: true,
    sameSite: 'lax',
    secure: process.env.COOKIE_SECURE === 'true',
    maxAge: JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS * 1000, // in milliseconds for Express
    path: '/',
  };
}
  • lines 4–21: the comment explains why the token is stored in a cookie and the purpose of each of its options (see example 25);
  • line 28: the key, read from [.env]. The default value should only be used during development;
  • lines 30–32: the token’s lifetime: two hours by default;
  • lines 34–42: the cookie options, grouped in one place (they are used for logging in and modifying a patient’s account). [secure] is enabled only in production, where the site is served as HTTPS; [maxAge] is in milliseconds.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Authentication logic:
//    - validerUtilisateur(): verifies a username/password pair;
//    - creerJeton(        ) : generates the JWT token for a validated user;
//    - lireJeton(         ) : verifies a token (login page: if
//                             the user is already logged in, there’s no need to
//                             ask for their password again).
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { JwtService } from '@nestjs/jwt';
import * as bcrypt from 'bcryptjs';
import { UserRepository } from '../repositories/user.repository';
import { User } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { JwtPayload } from './jwt.strategy';

@Injectable()
export class AuthService {
  constructor(
    private readonly userRepository: UserRepository,
    private readonly jwtService: JwtService,
  ) {}

  async validerUtilisateur(login: string, password: string): Promise<User | null> {
    const user = await this.userRepository.findByLogin(login);
    if (user === null) {
      return null;
    }
    return (await bcrypt.compare(password, user.password)) ? user : null;
  }

  creerJeton(user: User): string {
    const payload: JwtPayload = { sub: user.id, login: user.login, nom: user.nom, role: user.role };
    return this.jwtService.sign(payload);
  }

   // returns the token’s contents if it is valid (correct signature, not
   // expired), null otherwise
  lireJeton(jeton: string | undefined): JwtPayload | null {
    if (!jeton) {
      return null;
    }
    try {
      return this.jwtService.verify<JwtPayload>(jeton);
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }
}
  • lines 26–32: the account if the username and password are correct ([bcrypt.compare]), [null] otherwise;
  • lines 34–37: the token, which contains the ID, username, display name, and role;
  • lines 41–50: [jwtService.verify] verifies a token’s signature and expiration date, and throws an exception if it is invalid. This method is used by unprotected pages (the login page) that want to determine whether the user is already logged in.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/jwt.strategy.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The Passport policy that authenticates the protected request CHAQUE from the
// token JWT. The only difference from the server JSON is that the token is read from the
// [rdvmedecins_jwt] cookie (see auth.constants.ts) instead of the
// "Authorization: Bearer ...".
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PassportStrategy } from '@nestjs/passport';
import { Request } from 'express';
import { ExtractJwt, Strategy } from 'passport-jwt';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { COOKIE_JWT, JWT_SECRET } from './auth.constants';

//—which is where the token DANS is stored when it is generated (see AuthService).
// The displayed name is also included there, so that the navigation bar can
// display it without querying the database on every page.
export interface JwtPayload {
  sub: number; // the user ID (convention: JWT)
  login: string;
  nom: string;
  role: Role;
}

// what request.user will contain once the token is verified
export interface UtilisateurConnecte {
  userId: number;
  login: string;
  nom: string;
  role: Role;
}

@Injectable()
export class JwtStrategy extends PassportStrategy(Strategy, 'jwt') {
  constructor() {
    super({
       // fromExtractors([...]): we provide NOTRE, the extraction function for the
       // token—here, reading a cookie (req.cookies is populated by the
       // cookie-parser middleware; see main.ts).
      jwtFromRequest: ExtractJwt.fromExtractors([(req: Request) => req?.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT] ?? null]),
      ignoreExpiration: false,
      secretOrKey: JWT_SECRET,
    });
  }

  validate(payload: JwtPayload): UtilisateurConnecte {
    return { userId: payload.sub, login: payload.login, nom: payload.nom, role: payload.role };
  }
}
  • lines 20–25: the token’s contents;
  • lines 28–33: what [req.user] will contain;
  • lines 38–45: the token is read from the cookie; if it has expired or is incorrectly signed, it is rejected;
  • lines 48–50: the token’s content becomes [req.user].

// =========================================================================
// auth/roles.decorator.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// @Roles('ADMIN') is a MAISON decorator (we write it ourselves,
// unlike @Get, @Post, and @Injectable provided by NestJS): it
// simply attaches metadata ("this method requires such-and-such a role") to
// the method it decorates, without performing any checks itself—that’s RolesGuard
// (see roles.guard.ts) that will read this metadata and perform the check.
//
// SetMetadata(key, value) is the low-level function of NestJS that allows
// to write this kind of "custom" decorator: we use it here so we don’t
// have to repeat the string 'roles' throughout the code.
// =========================================================================

import { SetMetadata } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';

export const ROLES_KEY = 'roles';
export const Roles = (...roles: Role[]) => SetMetadata(ROLES_KEY, roles);

Line 19: the [@Roles(...)] decorator (see Example 26). Its parameters are of type [Role]: [@Roles('ADMIM')] (typo) is rejected by the compiler.

docs.title: 11.12.6. src/auth/roles.guard.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/roles.guard.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Second level of verification, APRÈS JwtAuthGuard: this one verifies
// only that the user is properly authenticated (a valid JWT token); RolesGuard
// also verifies that the role of the logged-in user (request.user.role,
// submitted by JwtStrategy) is indeed among those required by @Roles(...)
// on the target method.
//
// Unchanged compared to the server JSON, except for the error destination:
// the ForbiddenException exception raised here is converted to PAGE "403 - access
// denied" by HtmlExceptionFilter (see web/html-exception.filter.ts).
//
// This is essentially equivalent to the Spring Security rule:
//    http.authorizeRequests().antMatchers(...).hasRole("ADMIN")
// but applied here method by method rather than URL by URL, thanks to the
// the combination of a decorator (@Roles) and Reflector (which can parse the metadata
// set by a decorator).
// =========================================================================

import { CanActivate, ExecutionContext, ForbiddenException, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core';
import { ROLES_KEY } from './roles.decorator';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { UtilisateurConnecte } from './jwt.strategy';

@Injectable()
export class RolesGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(private readonly reflector: Reflector) {}

  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
     // reads the metadata set by @Roles(...) on the target method—
     // getAllAndOverride first searches the method, then the class.
    const rolesRequis = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<Role[]>(ROLES_KEY, [context.getHandler(), context.getClass()]);

     // No @Roles(...) metadata on this method: no restrictions
     // additional role (JwtAuthGuard, on the other hand, will have already required
     // valid authentication, regardless of the role).
    if (!rolesRequis || rolesRequis.length === 0) {
      return true;
    }

     // request.user was submitted by JwtStrategy.validate() (see jwt.strategy.ts) -
     // RolesGuard therefore executes TOUJOURS after JwtAuthGuard (see their order
     // in @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RolesGuard), see src/web/controllers/).
    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest<{ user: UtilisateurConnecte }>();
    const utilisateur = request.user;

    if (!rolesRequis.includes(utilisateur.role)) {
      throw new ForbiddenException(
        `le rôle [${utilisateur.role}] ne permet pas cette action (rôle requis : ${rolesRequis.join(', ')})`,
      );
    }
    return true;
  }
}

The role mapping is identical to that in Example 26.

docs.title: 11.12.7. src/auth/captcha.service.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/captcha.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A CAPTCHA ("test to distinguish a human from a robot") generated by the
// server itself, without an external service: the svg-captcha library
// draws a few distorted characters, obscured by lines, in an
// image SVG. A human can read them easily; a bot that simply
// sending forms over and over again cannot do so.
//
// How it works:
//    1. generer() generates a random text, turns it into an image, and stores the
//       correct answer EN MÉMOIRE DU SERVEUR, under a random ID;
//    2. The page displays the image and places the identifier in a hidden field
//       in the form (the response itself never leaves the server);
//    3. verify(id, input) compares the input to the expected response, then
//       OUBLIE this CAPTCHA: each image is used only once, so a bot cannot
//       reuse a response that has already been found.
//
// Assumed limitation: the memory of a single Node process. With multiple
// servers behind a load balancer, shared storage would be required
// shared storage (Redis, database...).
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto';
import * as svgCaptcha from 'svg-captcha';

// Image validity period: you have 10 minutes to fill out the form
const DUREE_VIE_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;
// memory safeguard: after that, the oldest captchas are discarded
const MAX_CAPTCHAS = 10_000;

export interface Captcha {
  id: string; // to be placed in the hidden field "captchaId" of the form
  svg: string; // the image, to be inserted as-is into the page
}

@Injectable()
export class CaptchaService {
   // id -> { expected response, expiration date }. A Map preserves the order
   // of insertion: its earliest entries are the oldest.
  private readonly enAttente = new Map<string, { texte: string; expire: number }>();

  generer(): Captcha {
    this.purger();
    const { text, data } = svgCaptcha.create({
      size: 5, // 5 characters
      noise: 3, // 3 scrambling characters
      color: true,
      background: '#f5f7fa',
       // characters that are too easily confused with one another: excluded
      ignoreChars: '0oO1iIlL',
    });
    const id = randomUUID();
    this.enAttente.set(id, { texte: text.toLowerCase(), expire: Date.now() + DUREE_VIE_MS });
    return { id, svg: data };
  }

   // true if [saisie] is the correct answer to the captcha [id] (without taking
   // of uppercase letters). The CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases.
  verifier(id: unknown, saisie: unknown): boolean {
    if (typeof id !== 'string' || typeof saisie !== 'string') {
      return false;
    }
    const attendu = this.enAttente.get(id);
    this.enAttente.delete(id);
    return attendu !== undefined && attendu.expire > Date.now() && attendu.texte === saisie.trim().toLowerCase();
  }

  private purger(): void {
    const maintenant = Date.now();
    for (const [id, { expire }] of this.enAttente) {
      if (expire <= maintenant || this.enAttente.size >= MAX_CAPTCHAS) {
        this.enAttente.delete(id);
      }
    }
  }
}
  • Lines 29–31: Compared to Example 27, a CAPTCHA has a lifespan (ten minutes), and the number of CAPTCHAs in memory is capped: a bot requesting the login page millions of times would not be able to exhaust the server’s memory;
  • line 42: a [Map] preserves the order of insertion: its earliest entries are the oldest;
  • lines 44–57: the image, its expected response (in lowercase), and its expiration date;
  • lines 61–68: The answer is compared without regard to case; the CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases;
  • lines 70–77: Expired CAPTCHAs are discarded, as are the oldest ones if the limit is reached.

docs.title: 11.12.8. src/auth/limiteur-tentatives.service.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/limiteur-tentatives.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Second line of defense against bots (the first is the CAPTCHA): on COMPTE
// attempts, and once a certain threshold is exceeded, BLOQUE for a while.
//
//    - Login: After LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS failed attempts (incorrect CAPTCHA or incorrect
//      password) for the same login from the same IP address IP, this pair
//      is blocked for LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES minutes. The same IP address IP is also
//      blocked if it accumulates 5 times as many failed attempts, across all logins (a
//      bot that tries thousands of different logins);
//    - account creation: no more than INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE accounts created
//      per hour from the same IP address IP.
//
// Caution in the classroom: all computers frequently access the Internet
// via the MÊME address IP. This is why the connection block applies
// primarily on the pair (IP, login)—a student who enters the wrong password
// does not block their neighbors—and why the thresholds are adjustable
// in the .env file.
//
// As with the CAPTCHA, the counters reside in the process’s memory.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';

interface Compteur {
  nombre: number; // Attempts counted in the current window
  debut: number; // start of the counting window (ms)
  bloqueJusqua: number; // 0 if not blocked
}

const MINUTE = 60 * 1000;

function entierEnv(nom: string, defaut: number): number {
  const valeur = parseInt(process.env[nom] ?? '', 10);
  return Number.isInteger(valeur) && valeur > 0 ? valeur : defaut;
}

@Injectable()
export class LimiteurTentativesService {
  private readonly compteurs = new Map<string, Compteur>();

  private readonly maxEchecsLogin = entierEnv('LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS', 5);
  private readonly dureeBlocageLogin = entierEnv('LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES', 15) * MINUTE;
  private readonly maxInscriptions = entierEnv('INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE', 10);

   // ---------------------------------------------------------------- connection

   // number of remaining minutes of lockout (0 = attempt is allowed)
  minutesBlocageLogin(ip: string, login: string): number {
    return Math.max(this.minutesRestantes(cleLogin(ip, login)), this.minutesRestantes(cleIp(ip)));
  }

  echecLogin(ip: string, login: string): void {
    this.compter(cleLogin(ip, login), this.maxEchecsLogin, this.dureeBlocageLogin, this.dureeBlocageLogin);
    this.compter(cleIp(ip), this.maxEchecsLogin * 5, this.dureeBlocageLogin, this.dureeBlocageLogin);
  }

   // A successful connection resets the CE login counter
  reussiteLogin(ip: string, login: string): void {
    this.compteurs.delete(cleLogin(ip, login));
  }

   // ---------------------------------------------------------------- registration

  minutesBlocageInscription(ip: string): number {
    return this.minutesRestantes(`inscription|${ip}`);
  }

  inscriptionReussie(ip: string): void {
     // one-hour window; once the quota is reached, access is blocked until the end of the hour
    this.compter(`inscription|${ip}`, this.maxInscriptions, 60 * MINUTE, 60 * MINUTE);
  }

   // ---------------------------------------------------------------- standard mechanism

  private minutesRestantes(cle: string): number {
    const c = this.compteurs.get(cle);
    const reste = c ? c.bloqueJusqua - Date.now() : 0;
    return reste > 0 ? Math.ceil(reste / MINUTE) : 0;
  }

   // counts as one attempt; if the threshold is reached within the window, access is blocked
  private compter(cle: string, max: number, fenetre: number, blocage: number): void {
    const maintenant = Date.now();
    this.purger(maintenant);
    let c = this.compteurs.get(cle);
    if (!c || maintenant - c.debut > fenetre) {
      c = { nombre: 0, debut: maintenant, bloqueJusqua: 0 };
      this.compteurs.set(cle, c);
    }
    c.nombre++;
    if (c.nombre >= max) {
      c.bloqueJusqua = maintenant + blocage;
      c.nombre = 0; // after the block, the counter resets to zero
      c.debut = c.bloqueJusqua;
    }
  }

   // Counters that are no longer in use (neither blocked nor recent) are ignored
  private purger(maintenant: number): void {
    if (this.compteurs.size < 1000) {
      return;
    }
    for (const [cle, c] of this.compteurs) {
      if (c.bloqueJusqua < maintenant && maintenant - c.debut > 60 * MINUTE) {
        this.compteurs.delete(cle);
      }
    }
  }
}

function cleLogin(ip: string, login: string): string {
  return `login|${ip}|${login.trim().toLowerCase()}`;
}

function cleIp(ip: string): string {
  return `ip|${ip}`;
}
  • lines 26–30: an attempt counter, with the start of its counting window and its lockout end date;
  • lines 34–37: a threshold read from [.env], with a default value;
  • lines 50–52: The lock applies to the pair (address IP, login), and to address IP alone when it accumulates a large number of failed attempts, across all logins. In a classroom, all workstations often connect via the same address, IP: a student who enters the wrong password should not lock out their neighbors;
  • lines 54–57: one failed attempt counts toward both keys;
  • lines 66–68 and 70–73: the number of accounts created per hour from the same address, IP, is limited;
  • lines 84–98: counting. An expired window resets to zero; when the threshold is reached, the key is blocked;
  • lines 101–110: clearing old counters to prevent keys from accumulating indefinitely in memory;
  • lines 113–118: generation of keys for [Map].

docs.title: 11.12.9. src/auth/passe-inscription.service.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/passe-inscription.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The "pass" for creating an account.
//
// To open the “Create a Customer Account” page, you must first have
// entered the CAPTCHA from the authentication page (see
// InscriptionController, POST /registration/access). The server then issues
// then issues a token:
//    - a random identifier, stored in a cookie named httpOnly;
//    - valid for 15 minutes (enough time to fill out the form, even
//      you have to try several times after data entry errors);
//    - expires as soon as an account is created: UN captcha solved = UN account
//      anymore. A bot cannot create accounts in bulk.
//
// Without a valid passcode, GET and POST /registration redirect to the
// authentication page: typing URL /registration directly does not allow
// bypass the CAPTCHA.
//
// Like the CAPTCHA, the tokens reside in the process’s memory.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto';
import { CookieOptions } from 'express';

export const COOKIE_PASSE_INSCRIPTION = 'rdvmedecins_inscription';

const DUREE_VIE_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;
const MAX_PASSES = 10_000;

@Injectable()
export class PasseInscriptionService {
   // ID -> expiration date
  private readonly passes = new Map<string, number>();

   // Issues a new token; returns its ID
  emettre(): string {
    this.purger();
    const id = randomUUID();
    this.passes.set(id, Date.now() + DUREE_VIE_MS);
    return id;
  }

   // true if [id] is an existing, unexpired token
  estValide(id: unknown): boolean {
    if (typeof id !== 'string') {
      return false;
    }
    const expire = this.passes.get(id);
    return expire !== undefined && expire > Date.now();
  }

   // the pass has been used: discard it
  consommer(id: unknown): void {
    if (typeof id === 'string') {
      this.passes.delete(id);
    }
  }

  optionsCookie(): CookieOptions {
    return { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax', maxAge: DUREE_VIE_MS, path: '/inscription' };
  }

  private purger(): void {
    const maintenant = Date.now();
    for (const [id, expire] of this.passes) {
      if (expire <= maintenant || this.passes.size >= MAX_PASSES) {
        this.passes.delete(id);
      }
    }
  }
}

Creating a customer account is available from the login page, provided the CAPTCHA has been solved. Therefore, a request (the registration form) must know that a previous request solved the CAPTCHA. This is the role of the token:

  • lines 38–43: a random identifier, valid for 15 minutes, stored in memory; it will be saved in a cookie;
  • lines 46–52: the registration form is displayed and accepted only with a valid token;
  • lines 55–59: Creating an account consumes the token: a solved CAPTCHA entitles the user to one account, and no more;
  • lines 61–63: The option ***[path: '/inscription']*** restricts the sending of the cookie to URL values that begin with ***[/inscription]***.

docs.title: 11.12.10. src/auth/auth.controller.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.controller.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The NON routes protected by the connection:
//    GE T         / redirects to the role’s home page (or to /login)
//    GE T /log  in displays the login form (with its CAPTCHA)
//    POST /logi  n checks the number of failed login attempts, CAPTCHA, and username/password
//    POST /logou t deletes the token cookie
//
// The JSON server used a "local" Passport guard for POST /login:
// if authentication failed, it would respond directly with a 401, which is appropriate for a
// JavaScript client. A HTML page, on the other hand, must RÉAFFICHER the form
// with an error message: we therefore call AuthService ourselves.
//
// Spam protection, in that order (see captcha.service.ts and
// limiteur-tentatives.service.ts):
//    1. Too many recent failed attempts for this login from this address IP?
//       -> Immediate rejection, without even checking the password;
//    2. Incorrect CAPTCHA answer? -> Rejected (counted as a failed attempt);
//    3. Only then is the password verified.
// The password for a rejected attempt is not verified in steps
// 1 or 2: a bot therefore cannot learn anything by repeatedly trying.
// =========================================================================

import { Body, Controller, Get, HttpCode, Post, Query, Req, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { AuthService } from './auth.service';
import { CaptchaService } from './captcha.service';
import { LimiteurTentativesService } from './limiteur-tentatives.service';
import { COOKIE_JWT, optionsCookieJwt } from './auth.constants';
import { Role } from '../entities/user.entity';

// the home page for each role, immediately after logging in
export function pageAccueil(role: Role): string {
  return role === 'USER' ? '/mon-espace' : '/agenda';
}

@Controller()
export class AuthController {
  constructor(
    private readonly authService: AuthService,
    private readonly captchaService: CaptchaService,
    private readonly limiteur: LimiteurTentativesService,
  ) {}

  @Get()
  accueil(@Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response): void {
    const jeton = this.authService.lireJeton(req.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT]);
    res.redirect(jeton ? pageAccueil(jeton.role) : '/login');
  }

   // GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the
   // login (used immediately after creating an account; see InscriptionController)
  @Get('login')
  afficherLogin(@Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response, @Query('login') login?: string): void {
     // already logged in (token still valid): goes directly to the home page
    const jeton = this.authService.lireJeton(req.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT]);
    if (jeton !== null) {
      return res.redirect(pageAccueil(jeton.role));
    }
    this.afficherFormulaire(res, typeof login === 'string' ? login.slice(0, 30) : '');
  }

   // @HttpCode(200): By default, NestJS returns a 201 (Created) response to a POST request—which
   // doesn’t make sense when submitting the form (a redirect, on the other hand,
   // imposes its own code anyway, 302).
  @Post('login')
  @HttpCode(200)
  async seConnecter(
    @Body() body: { login?: string; password?: string; captchaId?: string; captcha?: string },
    @Req() req: Request,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const login = (body.login ?? '').trim();
    const password = body.password ?? '';
    const ip = req.ip ?? 'inconnue';

     // 1. Too many recent failures?
    const minutes = this.limiteur.minutesBlocageLogin(ip, login);
    if (minutes > 0) {
      return this.afficherFormulaire(res, login, 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', { minutes: String(minutes) });
    }

     // 2. The CAPTCHA
    if (!this.captchaService.verifier(body.captchaId, body.captcha)) {
      this.limiteur.echecLogin(ip, login);
      return this.afficherFormulaire(res, login, 'ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA');
    }

     // 3. the password
    const user = login && password ? await this.authService.validerUtilisateur(login, password) : null;
    if (user === null) {
      this.limiteur.echecLogin(ip, login);
      return this.afficherFormulaire(res, login, 'LOGIN.ERROR');
    }

    this.limiteur.reussiteLogin(ip, login);
    res.cookie(COOKIE_JWT, this.authService.creerJeton(user), optionsCookieJwt());
    res.redirect(pageAccueil(user.role));
  }

   // Logout via POST (not via a simple link GET): a third-party site
   // log the user out without their knowledge (see sameSite, auth.constants.ts)
  @Post('logout')
  seDeconnecter(@Res() res: Response): void {
    res.clearCookie(COOKIE_JWT, { path: '/' });
    res.redirect('/login');
  }

   // the form, always with a NOUVEAU CAPTCHA (each image is used only once)
  private afficherFormulaire(
    res: Response,
    login: string,
    erreur?: string,
    erreurParams?: Record<string, string>,
  ): void {
    res.render('login', {
      titrePage: 'LOGIN.TITLE',
      login, // the entered username is displayed again, but never the password
      captcha: this.captchaService.generer(),
      erreur,
      erreurParams,
    });
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 34–36: The home page depends on the user’s role: “My Account” for patients, the calendar for everyone else;
  • lines 46–50: The site root redirects depending on whether the user is logged in or not. Since the route is not protected by the guard, the token is verified by [lireJeton];
  • lines 54–62: A user who is already logged in is sent to their home page. The parameter [login] pre-fills the field (after an account is created). [slice(0, 30)] limits its length: data from the request is never used without precautions;
  • lines 69–73: the login process, in order: potential lockout, CAPTCHA, then password (see Example 27). [req.ip] is the client’s IP address. If successful: counter reset to zero, cookie set, redirection to the role’s home page;
  • lines 104–108: logout;
  • lines 111–116: the login page, always with a new CAPTCHA. The error is a translation key, along with its parameters (the number of minutes of lockout).

// =========================================================================
// auth/auth.module.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The authentication module. It is EXPORTE:
//    - UserRepository, which the business layer needs (to create, modify,
//      delete a doctor’s or client’s account—see metier.service.ts);
//    - AuthService, CaptchaService, LimiteurTentativesService, and
//      PasseInscriptionService, also used by the "Create an Account"
//      and “Manage My Account” (src/web/).
// =========================================================================

import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { JwtModule } from '@nestjs/jwt';
import { PassportModule } from '@nestjs/passport';
import { TypeOrmModule } from '@nestjs/typeorm';
import { User } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { UserRepository } from '../repositories/user.repository';
import { AuthService } from './auth.service';
import { AuthController } from './auth.controller';
import { JwtStrategy } from './jwt.strategy';
import { CaptchaService } from './captcha.service';
import { LimiteurTentativesService } from './limiteur-tentatives.service';
import { PasseInscriptionService } from './passe-inscription.service';
import { JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS, JWT_SECRET } from './auth.constants';

@Module({
  imports: [
    TypeOrmModule.forFeature([User]),
    PassportModule,
    JwtModule.register({
      secret: JWT_SECRET,
      signOptions: { expiresIn: JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS },
    }),
  ],
  controllers: [AuthController],
  providers: [
    AuthService,
    UserRepository,
    JwtStrategy,
    CaptchaService,
    LimiteurTentativesService,
    PasseInscriptionService,
  ],
  exports: [UserRepository, AuthService, CaptchaService, LimiteurTentativesService, PasseInscriptionService],
})
export class AuthModule {}

docs.text: Before we look at the controllers, here’s what they have in common: translation, the context for each page, the interceptor, the exception filter, the list cache, and the helpers.

docs.title: 11.13.1. src/web/i18n.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/i18n.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// French/English translation of the interface.
//
// The Angular client was loading its dictionaries (public/i18n/fr.json and
// en.json) into NAVIGATEUR using @ngx-translate. Here, the pages are
// generated on the SERVEUR: they are therefore the same dictionaries (same
// keys, supplemented), but read only once by the server at startup.
// A Handlebars view resolves a key using the helper {{t 'CLE'}}
// (see views/helpers-handlebars.ts), which is equivalent to the `| translate` pipe.
// =========================================================================

import { readFileSync } from 'fs';
import { join } from 'path';
import { DOSSIER_I18N } from '../config/chemins';

export type Langue = 'fr' | 'en';
export const LANGUES: Langue[] = ['fr', 'en'];
export const LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT: Langue = 'fr';

// A dictionary is a nested JSON object: { "LOGIN": { "TITLE": "Login" } }
type Dictionnaire = { [cle: string]: string | Dictionnaire };

const dictionnaires: Record<Langue, Dictionnaire> = {
  fr: JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(DOSSIER_I18N, 'fr.json'), 'utf-8')),
  en: JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(DOSSIER_I18N, 'en.json'), 'utf-8')),
};

export function estUneLangue(valeur: unknown): valeur is Langue {
  return typeof valeur === 'string' && (LANGUES as string[]).includes(valeur);
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// translate('fr', 'MEDECINS.ADDED', { name: 'Marie PELISSIER' })
//    -> searches for MEDECINS and then ADDED in the French dictionary, and replaces
//       {name} with its value. A key that is missing from the requested language is
//       searched for in French; if it is missing everywhere, the key itself is displayed
//       (this allows us to immediately spot an omission in the dictionaries).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function traduire(langue: Langue, cle: string, params: Record<string, unknown> = {}): string {
  const texte = chercher(dictionnaires[langue], cle) ?? chercher(dictionnaires[LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT], cle) ?? cle;
  return texte.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (tout, nom: string) => (nom in params ? String(params[nom]) : tout));
}

function chercher(dictionnaire: Dictionnaire, cle: string): string | null {
  let noeud: string | Dictionnaire | undefined = dictionnaire;
  for (const morceau of cle.split('.')) {
    if (typeof noeud !== 'object' || noeud === null) {
      return null;
    }
    noeud = noeud[morceau];
  }
  return typeof noeud === 'string' ? noeud : null;
}

The translation module from Example 22, with one clarification (line 42): if a key is missing from the English dictionary, it is looked up in the French dictionary; if it is missing from both, the key itself is displayed.

docs.title: 11.13.2. src/web/contexte-vue.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/contexte-vue.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// What TOUTES the pages need to know, regardless of the path
// that displays them: the interface language, any “flash” message to
// display, and the logged-in user (for the navigation bar).
//
// Express provides [res.locals] for this purpose: an object attached to the response, in which
// the content is AUTOMATIQUEMENT merged with the template for each view at the
// time of res.render(...). Controllers therefore do not have to repeat this
// information in each of their models.
//
// Reminder: the Angular client stored this information in the browser
// (signals + localStorage). A server HTML, on the other hand, must retrieve it at
// CHAQUE request—in this case, in cookies.
// =========================================================================

import { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import { Langue, LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT, estUneLangue } from './i18n';
import { UtilisateurConnecte } from '../auth/jwt.strategy';

export const COOKIE_LANGUE = 'rdvmedecins_langue';
export const COOKIE_FLASH = 'rdvmedecins_flash';

// a message to be displayed UNE times on the next page
export interface MessageFlash {
  type: 'success' | 'danger'; // Bootstrap classes `alert-success` / `alert-danger`
  cle: string; // translation key
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

// the logged-in user, as seen by the views
export interface UtilisateurVue {
  login: string;
  nom: string;
  role: string;
  estAdmin: boolean; // ADMIN: Doctors / Clients menus
  estPatient: boolean; // USER: My Account menu
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Express middleware, executed on all routes (see main.ts):
//    - res.locals.lan g: selected language (cookie), French by default;
//    - res.locals.flash: any flash message, which is cleared
//                         immediately (it should only be displayed once);
//    - res.locals.chemin: the requested URL (active menu in the navigation bar).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function contexteVueMiddleware(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
  res.locals.lang = langueDe(req);
  res.locals.chemin = req.path;
  res.locals.flash = null;
  res.locals.utilisateur = null;

  const brut = req.cookies?.[COOKIE_FLASH];
  if (brut) {
    try {
      res.locals.flash = JSON.parse(brut) as MessageFlash;
    } catch {
       // unreadable cookie: ignored
    }
    res.clearCookie(COOKIE_FLASH);
  }
  next();
}

export function langueDe(req: Request): Langue {
  const valeur = req.cookies?.[COOKIE_LANGUE];
  return estUneLangue(valeur) ? valeur : LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT;
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// sets a flash message, which will be displayed by the PROCHAINE page. This is the
// natural extension of the “Post / Redirect / Get” pattern used by all
// forms in the application: a successful POST does not generate a page; it
// redirects (302) to a GET page—if the user then reloads that
// page (F5), the browser does not resubmit the form a second time.
// The message, however, must survive the redirect: a short-lived cookie
// will do the trick.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function flash(res: Response, message: MessageFlash): void {
  res.cookie(COOKIE_FLASH, JSON.stringify(message), { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax', maxAge: 60_000 });
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// exposes the logged-in user (request.user, set by JwtStrategy) to the
// views. Called by UtilisateurVueInterceptor (normal routes) and by
// HtmlExceptionFilter (error pages).
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
export function exposerUtilisateur(req: Request, res: Response): void {
  const user = (req as Request & { user?: UtilisateurConnecte }).user;
  if (!user) {
    return;
  }
  const utilisateur: UtilisateurVue = {
    login: user.login,
    nom: user.nom,
    role: user.role,
    estAdmin: user.role === 'ADMIN',
    estPatient: user.role === 'USER',
  };
  res.locals.utilisateur = utilisateur;
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 22–23: the names of the language and flash message cookies;
  • lines 26–30: a flash message: a type (success or error), a translation key, and its parameters. It is stored in the cookie as JSON;
  • lines 33–39: the logged-in user, as seen by the views. The booleans [estAdmin] and [estPatient] prevent the views from comparing strings;
  • lines 48–64: the middleware executed before any route (see examples 20 and 22): the language, the path (for the active menu), and the flash message, which is read and then cleared. [JSON.parse] is protected by a [try]: a manually modified cookie should not cause the page to fail;
  • lines 66–69: the language, based on its cookie;
  • lines 80–82: displays a flash message (see example 20);
  • Lines 89–102: Copies the logged-in user ([req.user]) to [res.locals] for the navigation bar. This function is not called by the middleware: the middleware runs before the guards, and therefore before [req.user] exists (see Chapter 7). It is called by the following interceptor and by the exception filter.

docs.title: 11.13.3. src/web/utilisateur-vue.interceptor.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/utilisateur-vue.interceptor.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Why an interceptor and not just the middleware from
// contexte-vue.ts? Because the execution context matters:
//
//      middleware -> guards (JwtAuthGuard...) -> interceptors -> controller
//
// The guard JwtAuthGuard registers request.user: a middleware passes through
// too early to see it. An interceptor, on the other hand, executes APRÈS the guards and
// AVANT the controller—the right time to copy the logged-in user
// to res.locals, where all views will find it.
// =========================================================================

import { CallHandler, ExecutionContext, Injectable, NestInterceptor } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { Observable } from 'rxjs';
import { exposerUtilisateur } from './contexte-vue';

@Injectable()
export class UtilisateurVueInterceptor implements NestInterceptor {
  intercept(context: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler): Observable<unknown> {
    const http = context.switchToHttp();
    exposerUtilisateur(http.getRequest<Request>(), http.getResponse<Response>());
    return next.handle();
  }
}

Lines 22–26: An interceptor runs after the guards and before the action: this is the right time to expose the user passed by [JwtAuthGuard]. It has nothing to do after the action: it returns [next.handle()] directly.

docs.title: 11.13.4. src/web/html-exception.filter.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/html-exception.filter.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An "exception filter" NestJS catches any exception that has not been
// handled by the controller code. By default, NestJS responds with JSON
// ({"statusCode":403,"message":...})—perfect for the JSON server, but
// unreadable in a browser. Instead, this filter generates a response
// suitable for a HTML application:
//
//    401 (not logged in, or token expired) -> redirect to /login
//    403 (insufficient rol             e) -> "Access Denied" error page
//    404 (page not foun                d) -> "Page Not Found" error page
//    400 (invalid parameter)            -> "Invalid Request" error page
//    all others                        -> 500 error page
//
// @Catch() without arguments: the filter catches TOUTES exceptions. It is
// registered once for the entire application in main.ts.
// =========================================================================

import { ArgumentsHost, Catch, ExceptionFilter, HttpException, HttpStatus, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { COOKIE_JWT } from '../auth/auth.constants';
import { exposerUtilisateur, flash } from './contexte-vue';

const MESSAGES: Record<number, string> = {
  [HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST]: 'ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST',
  [HttpStatus.FORBIDDEN]: 'ERRORS.FORBIDDEN',
  [HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND]: 'ERRORS.NOT_FOUND',
};

@Catch()
export class HtmlExceptionFilter implements ExceptionFilter {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(HtmlExceptionFilter.name);

  catch(exception: unknown, host: ArgumentsHost): void {
    const http = host.switchToHttp();
    const req = http.getRequest<Request>();
    const res = http.getResponse<Response>();

    const status = exception instanceof HttpException ? exception.getStatus() : HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;

    if (status === HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED) {
       // A cookie was present but is no longer valid: the session has expired
      if (req.cookies?.[COOKIE_JWT]) {
        res.clearCookie(COOKIE_JWT, { path: '/' });
        flash(res, { type: 'danger', cle: 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED' });
      }
      res.redirect('/login');
      return;
    }

    if (status >= 500) {
       // a true anomaly: a complete log is kept in the
       // server, without ever displaying it to the user
      this.logger.error(exception instanceof Error ? exception.stack : String(exception));
    }

     // The error page retains the logged-in user’s navigation bar
     // (if they are logged in—a 403 error occurs APRÈS during authentication)
    exposerUtilisateur(req, res);
    res.status(status).render('erreur', {
      titrePage: 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE',
      code: status,
      message: MESSAGES[status] ?? 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR',
    });
  }
}
  • lines 25–29: the message key for each error code;
  • lines 42–50: a 401 redirects to the login page. If a token cookie was present, it has expired (or the account has been deleted): it is deleted, and the user is notified via a pop-up message;
  • lines 52–56: A genuine error is logged in the server console, along with its call stack, but is never disclosed to the user: these details would assist an attacker;
  • lines 60–65: the error page, with the logged-in user’s navigation bar.

docs.title: 11.13.5. src/web/application-model.service.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// web/application-model.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The cache/frontend already present on the server JSON (equivalent to the
// [ApplicationModel] class from the Spring project): the lists of doctors and
// client lists are read once at startup and then served from memory.
//
// New feature: these lists can now CHANGER (the ADMIN adds,
// modify or delete doctors and clients). A cache that is
// is never updated would display outdated data: every write
// therefore goes through this service, which reloads the relevant list immediately afterward.
// This is the whole point of having an entry point UNIQUE to the
// business layer: the rule “write => reload the cache” is only enforced here.
// =========================================================================

import { Inject, Injectable, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common';
import { DonneesPersonne, IMetier, METIER_TOKEN } from '../metier/metier.interface';
import { Client } from '../entities/client.entity';
import { Medecin } from '../entities/medecin.entity';
import { Creneau } from '../entities/creneau.entity';
import { Rv } from '../entities/rv.entity';
import { AgendaMedecinJour } from '../domain/agenda-medecin-jour';

@Injectable()
export class ApplicationModelService implements IMetier, OnModuleInit {
  private medecins: Medecin[] = [];
  private clients: Client[] = [];

  constructor(@Inject(METIER_TOKEN) private readonly metier: IMetier) {}

   // If the database is inaccessible at startup, the exception shuts down the server
   // with an explicit message—which is clearer for an application HTML than
   // starting “empty” and displaying empty lists.
  async onModuleInit(): Promise<void> {
    await this.rechargerMedecins();
    await this.rechargerClients();
  }

  private async rechargerMedecins(): Promise<void> {
    this.medecins = await this.metier.getAllMedecins();
  }

  private async rechargerClients(): Promise<void> {
    this.clients = await this.metier.getAllClients();
  }

   // ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

  async getAllMedecins(): Promise<Medecin[]> {
    return this.medecins;
  }

  async getAllClients(): Promise<Client[]> {
    return this.clients;
  }

   // the doctor whose user account is [idUser]—used for preselection,
   // for a logged-in doctor, their own calendar
  getMedecinByUserId(idUser: number): Medecin | null {
    return this.medecins.find((m) => m.idUser === idUser) ?? null;
  }

   // ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

  getAllCreneaux(idMedecin: number): Promise<Creneau[]> {
    return this.metier.getAllCreneaux(idMedecin);
  }

  getRvMedecinJour(idMedecin: number, jour: string): Promise<Rv[]> {
    return this.metier.getRvMedecinJour(idMedecin, jour);
  }

  getClientById(id: number): Promise<Client | null> {
    return this.metier.getClientById(id);
  }

  getMedecinById(id: number): Promise<Medecin | null> {
    return this.metier.getMedecinById(id);
  }

  getRvById(id: number): Promise<Rv | null> {
    return this.metier.getRvById(id);
  }

  getCreneauById(id: number): Promise<Creneau | null> {
    return this.metier.getCreneauById(id);
