             value="{{valeurs.age}}" required>
      {{#if erreurs.age}}<div class="invalid-feedback">{{erreurs.age}}</div>{{/if}}
    </div>
  </div>
  <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Enregistrer</button>
  <a class="btn btn-link" href="/personnes">Retour à la liste</a>
</form>

Line 4: the hidden field that carries the record’s version. The view is used for adding and modifying records: its title and the submission URL ([action]) are provided by the controller. The views [liste.hbs] and [layout.hbs], along with the confirmation script, are the same as those in Examples 20 and 21.

docs.title: 9.1.7. Execution
docs.text:
Connection parameters are passed via environment variables if the default values are not suitable. Under [Windows] ([PowerShell]):

$env:DB_USERNAME="root"; $env:DB_PASSWORD=""; $env:DB_LOGGING="true"; npx nest start

The list:

An invalid form:

A homonym, written in lowercase and without accents: the business rule detects it, because MySQL compares based on the database's collation:

A successful addition, and the corresponding SQL orders ([DB_LOGGING=true]):

query: START TRANSACTION
query: SELECT `Personne`.`id` AS `Personne_id`, `Personne`.`version` AS `Personne_version`, `Personne`.`prenom` AS `Personne_prenom`, `Personne`.`nom` AS `Personne_nom`, `Personne`.`age` AS `Personne_age` FROM `personnes` `Personne` WHERE ((`Personne`.`prenom` = ?) AND (`Personne`.`nom` = ?) AND (`Personne`.`id` != ?)) LIMIT 1 -- PARAMETERS: ["Sylvie","Durand",0]
query: INSERT INTO `personnes`(`id`, `version`, `prenom`, `nom`, `age`) VALUES (DEFAULT, 1, ?, ?, ?) -- PARAMETERS: ["Sylvie","Durand",29]
query: SELECT `Personne`.`id` AS `Personne_id`, `Personne`.`version` AS `Personne_version` FROM `personnes` `Personne` WHERE `Personne`.`id` = ? -- PARAMETERS: [4]
query: COMMIT
query: SELECT `Personne`.`id` AS `Personne_id`, `Personne`.`version` AS `Personne_version`, `Personne`.`prenom` AS `Personne_prenom`, `Personne`.`nom` AS `Personne_nom`, `Personne`.`age` AS `Personne_age` FROM `personnes` `Personne` ORDER BY `Personne`.`nom` ASC, `Personne`.`prenom` ASC

We can see the transaction ([START TRANSACTION] ... [COMMIT]), the search for duplicates, the insertion with version 1, and then, after the redirection, the reading of the list. The optimistic lock: two forms are open on the same record; the first is saved (the version changes to 2); the second, which still has version 1, is rejected:

Deletion, with confirmation:

docs.title: 3. The Action Model
docs.text: An action requires information sent by the browser: the URL parameters ([?nom=martin&age=42]), form fields, and route parameters. The original course refers to all of this information as the action’s model. This chapter shows how [NestJS] provides it to the action, converts it to the correct type, and validates it.

docs.title: 3.1. Example 07: URL Parameters
docs.text:
The [src/parametres.controller.ts] file:

import { Controller, DefaultValuePipe, Get, ParseIntPipe, Query } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller('parametres')
export class ParametresController {
   // /settings/action01?name=martin
  @Get('action01')
  action01(@Query('nom') nom: string): string {
    return `nom = [${nom}], de type ${typeof nom}`;
  }

   // /settings/action02?age=42: a parameter is TOUJOURS a string
  @Get('action02')
  action02(@Query('age') age: number): string {
    return `age = [${age}], de type ${typeof age}`;
  }

   // /parameters/action03?age=42: ParseIntPipe converts (or rejects)
  @Get('action03')
  action03(@Query('age', ParseIntPipe) age: number): string {
    return `age = [${age}], de type ${typeof age}`;
  }

   // /parameters/action04?page=2: a default value if the parameter is missing
  @Get('action04')
  action04(@Query('page', new DefaultValuePipe(1), ParseIntPipe) page: number): string {
    return `page = [${page}], de type ${typeof page}`;
  }

   // /parameters/action05?name=martin&age=42: all parameters at once
  @Get('action05')
  action05(@Query() parametres: Record<string, string>): object {
    return parametres;
  }
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • Lines 6–9: [@Query('nom')] inserts the value of the [nom] parameter from URL (the part following [?], called the query string or [query string]);
  • lines 12–15: the parameter [age] is declared as type [number]... but this type is merely a declaration [TypeScript], which is removed at compile time. What we receive is always a string, as shown by the execution;
  • lines 18–21: [ParseIntPipe] is a pipe: an object that transforms (and validates) a parameter’s value before it reaches the action. Here, the string ['42'] becomes the number 42; a non-numeric string causes a 400 (Bad Request) error, without the action being executed;
  • lines 24–27: the pipes are chained together: [DefaultValuePipe(1)] replaces a missing parameter with 1, then [ParseIntPipe] converts it;
  • lines 30–33: [@Query()], without any arguments, injects an object containing all the parameters from URL.

The results:

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action01?nom=martin"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 30

nom = [martin], de type string

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action01"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 36

nom = [undefined], de type undefined

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action02?age=42"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 26

age = [42], de type string

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action03?age=42"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 26

age = [42], de type number

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action03?age=abc"

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 99

{"message":"Validation failed (numeric string is expected)","error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action04"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 26

page = [1], de type number

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action04?page=2"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 26

page = [2], de type number

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/parametres/action05?nom=martin&age=42"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 27

{"nom":"martin","age":"42"}

The quotation marks around URL are necessary when it contains the character [&], which has a specific meaning for the console. Note that:

  • a missing parameter is treated as [undefined];
  • a present parameter is a string, regardless of the declared type;
  • a pipe is used to convert and validate a parameter, and returns a 400 status code if the value is invalid.

docs.title: 3.2. Example 08: An action template described by a class
docs.text:
When an action has multiple parameters, they are described by a class, often called [DTO] ([Data Transfer Object]). Each field of the class has validation decorators provided by the [class-validator] library. These are equivalent to the attributes [[Required]], [[Range]]..., etc., of [ASP.NET MVC].

The [src/personne.dto.ts] file:

import { Type } from 'class-transformer';
import { IsEmail, IsIn, IsInt, IsNotEmpty, IsOptional, Length, Max, Min } from 'class-validator';

export class PersonneDto {
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'le nom est obligatoire' })
  @Length(2, 20, { message: 'le nom doit avoir de 2 à 20 caractères' })
  nom: string;

  @Type(() => Number)
  @IsInt({ message: "l'âge doit être un nombre entier" })
  @Min(0, { message: "l'âge doit être positif" })
  @Max(150, { message: "l'âge ne peut dépasser 150" })
  age: number;

  @IsIn(['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'], { message: 'titre inconnu' })
  titre: string;

  @IsOptional()
  @IsEmail({}, { message: 'adresse électronique invalide' })
  email?: string;
}

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 1: [@Type] comes from the [class-transformer] library, which converts the received data;
  • line 2: the validation decorators from [class-validator];
  • lines 5–7: the name is required ([@IsNotEmpty]) and must be between 2 and 20 characters long ([@Length]). Each decorator accepts a custom error message;
  • lines 9–13: [@Type(() => Number)] requires the received string to be converted to a number before validation: an integer ([@IsInt]) between 0 and 150 ([@Min], [@Max]);
  • lines 15–16: the title must be one of the values in a list;
  • lines 18–20: the email address is optional ([@IsOptional]); if present, it must be valid ([@IsEmail]).

The file [src/personnes.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Query } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PersonneDto } from './personne.dto';

@Controller('personnes')
export class PersonnesController {
   // /people/action01?name=martin&age=42&title=Mr
  @Get('action01')
  action01(@Query() personne: PersonneDto): object {
    return {
      personne,
      typeAge: typeof personne.age,
      estUnePersonneDto: personne instanceof PersonneDto,
    };
  }
}

line 8: the action receives a [PersonneDto]. The action returns the received person, their age type, and verifies that it is indeed an instance of the [PersonneDto] class.

To ensure that the class’s decorators are applied, validation must be enabled once and for all in [main.ts]:

The file [src/main.ts]:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { ValidationPipe } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
   // automatic validation of TOUS action templates described by a class
  app.useGlobalPipes(
    new ValidationPipe({
      transform: true, // converts the received strings to the declared types
      whitelist: true, // removes fields not declared in the class
    }),
  );
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Serveur démarré sur http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();
  • lines 8–13: A global pipe, [ValidationPipe], is applied to all parameters of all actions. For a parameter whose type is a class, it checks the constraints of its decorators;
  • line 10: [transform: true]: the action receives a true instance of [PersonneDto], whose fields have been converted ([@Type]);
  • line 11: [whitelist: true]: Parameters that do not correspond to any field in the class are removed.

A valid request with a parameter ([pirate]) that is not declared in the class:

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/personnes/action01?nom=martin&age=42&titre=Mr&pirate=1"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 95

{"personne":{"nom":"martin","age":42,"titre":"Mr"},"typeAge":"number","estUnePersonneDto":true}

The age has indeed become a number, and the parameter [pirate] has disappeared. An invalid query:

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/personnes/action01?nom=m&age=abc&titre=Dr&email=xx"

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 240

{"message":["le nom doit avoir de 2 à 20 caractères","l'âge ne peut dépasser 150","l'âge doit être positif","l'âge doit être un nombre entier","titre inconnu","adresse électronique invalide"],"error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}

[ValidationPipe] rejected the request with a 400 error, the body of which (JSON) lists the error messages. The action was not executed. The same result occurs without any parameters:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/people/action01

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 232

{"message":["le nom doit avoir de 2 à 20 caractères","le nom est obligatoire","l'âge ne peut dépasser 150","l'âge doit être positif","l'âge doit être un nombre entier","titre inconnu"],"error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}

This behavior is expected for a JSON server, queried by a [JavaScript] client that displays errors in its own way. For a HTML application, an error JSON makes no sense: we want to redisplay the form with its errors. The following example shows how to take control.

docs.title: 3.3. Example 09: Validation Performed by the Action
docs.text:
Example 09 does not have a global [ValidationPipe]. The action itself converts and validates the model, using the same decorators (the [personne.dto.ts] file is identical):

The [src/personnes.controller.ts] file:

import { Controller, Get, Query } from '@nestjs/common';
import { plainToInstance } from 'class-transformer';
import { validate } from 'class-validator';
import { PersonneDto } from './personne.dto';

@Controller('personnes')
export class PersonnesController {
   // no ValidationPipe here: the action receives the parameters BRUTS and
   // decides for itself what to do with errors
  @Get('action01')
  async action01(@Query() brut: Record<string, string>): Promise<string> {
     // 1. raw object -> instance of PersonneDto (including @Type conversions)
    const personne = plainToInstance(PersonneDto, brut);
     // 2. Constraint checking (@IsNotEmpty, @Min...)
    const erreurs = await validate(personne);
     // 3. A HTML page in both cases: no 400 error
    if (erreurs.length === 0) {
      return `<p>Bienvenue ${personne.titre} ${personne.nom} (${personne.age} ans)</p>`;
    }
    const items = erreurs
      .map((e) => `<li>${e.property} : ${Object.values(e.constraints ?? {}).join(', ')}</li>`)
      .join('');
    return `<p>Le formulaire contient des erreurs :</p><ul>${items}</ul>`;
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 11: the action receives the raw parameters: an object whose fields are all strings;
  • line 13: [plainToInstance] ([class-transformer]) creates an instance of [PersonneDto] from the raw object, applying the conversions ([@Type]);
  • line 15: [validate] ([class-validator]) checks all constraints. It returns an error array, which is empty if everything is OK. Each error indicates the problematic field ([property]) and the messages for the violated constraints ([constraints]);
  • lines 17–18: no errors—a welcome page;
  • lines 20–23: otherwise, a page listing the errors. In both cases, the response is a HTML page, with status code 200.

This is the technique that all forms in the case study will use (see Example 19).

docs.title: 3.4. Example 10: Multiple Parameters
docs.text:
A single parameter can appear multiple times in a request: this is the case with checkboxes on a form or a multiple-selection list ([?couleur=rouge&couleur=vert]).

The file [src/tableaux.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Query } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ChoixDto } from './choix.dto';

@Controller('tableaux')
export class TableauxController {
   // /tables/action01?color=red&color=green: what Express receives
  @Get('action01')
  action01(@Query('couleur') couleur: string | string[]): object {
    return { couleur, estUnTableau: Array.isArray(couleur) };
  }

   // /tables/action02?color=red: still a table thanks to ChoixDto
  @Get('action02')
  action02(@Query() choix: ChoixDto): object {
    return { couleurs: choix.couleur, nombre: choix.couleur.length };
  }
}

The [action01] action (lines 7–10) shows what an action receives:

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/tableaux/action01?couleur=rouge"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 40

{"couleur":"rouge","estUnTableau":false}

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/tableaux/action01?couleur=rouge&couleur=vert"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 48

{"couleur":["rouge","vert"],"estUnTableau":true}

The type depends on the number of values: a string for a single value, an array for multiple values. This is a common pitfall. The [ChoixDto] class handles both cases as an array:

The file [src/choix.dto.ts]:

import { Transform } from 'class-transformer';
import { ArrayMinSize, IsArray, IsIn } from 'class-validator';

export class ChoixDto {
   // ?color=red -> "red"; ?color=red&color=green -> ["rouge","vert"]
   // @Transform converts both cases into an array
  @Transform(({ value }) => (Array.isArray(value) ? value : [value]))
  @IsArray()
  @ArrayMinSize(1, { message: 'choisissez au moins une couleur' })
  @IsIn(['rouge', 'vert', 'bleu'], { each: true, message: 'couleur inconnue' })
  couleur: string[];
}
  • line 7: [@Transform] ([class-transformer]) applies a conversion function to the field: a single value is placed in an array;
  • line 8: the field must be an array...
  • line 9: ...with at least one element...
  • line 10: ... and each element ([each: true]) must be in the list.
curl -i "http://localhost:3000/tableaux/action02?couleur=rouge"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 33

{"couleurs":["rouge"],"nombre":1}

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/tableaux/action02?couleur=rouge&couleur=vert"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 40

{"couleurs":["rouge","vert"],"nombre":2}

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/tableaux/action02?couleur=rouge&couleur=noir"

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 71

{"message":["couleur inconnue"],"error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}

docs.title: 3.5. Example 11: Parameters of a POST request
docs.text:
A HTML form sent using the POST method places its fields in the request body, not in the URL. The [@Body] decorator then replaces [@Query]:

The file [src/post.controller.ts]:

import { Body, Controller, Headers, Post } from '@nestjs/common';
import { PersonneDto } from './personne.dto';

@Controller('post')
export class PostController {
   // the request body, as-is
  @Post('action01')
  action01(@Body() corps: Record<string, unknown>, @Headers('content-type') type: string): object {
    return { typeRecu: type, corps };
  }

   // a single field from the body
  @Post('action02')
  action02(@Body('nom') nom: string): string {
    return `nom = [${nom}]`;
  }

   // the body, converted and validated by the PersonneDto class
  @Post('action03')
  action03(@Body() personne: PersonneDto): object {
    return { personne, typeAge: typeof personne.age };
  }
}
  • lines 7–10: [@Body()] inserts the request body, which has already been decoded by [NestJS]. [@Headers('content-type')] inserts a request header: the body type;
  • lines 13–16: [@Body('nom')] inserts a single field from the body;
  • lines 19–22: as with [@Query], the body can be described by a class, validated by the global [ValidationPipe].

The [-d] option of [curl] sends a POST request with a body in the format of a HTML form ([application/x-www-form-urlencoded]):

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=42" http://localhost:3000/post/action01

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 84

{"typeRecu":"application/x-www-form-urlencoded","corps":{"nom":"martin","age":"42"}}

The same body in JSON format (this is what a client sends in [JavaScript] format):

curl -i -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"nom":"martin","age":42}' http://localhost:3000/post/action01

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 65

{"typeRecu":"application/json","corps":{"nom":"martin","age":42}}

[NestJS] decodes both formats. Note that “age” is a string in the first case (a HTML form carries only text) and a number in the second. The other two actions:

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=42" http://localhost:3000/post/action02

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 14

nom = [martin]

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=42&titre=Mme" http://localhost:3000/post/action03

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 71

{"personne":{"nom":"martin","age":42,"titre":"Mme"},"typeAge":"number"}

curl -i -d "nom=martin&age=200" http://localhost:3000/post/action03

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 99

{"message":["l'âge ne peut dépasser 150","titre inconnu"],"error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}

Code 201 (Created) is the default code for a POST for [NestJS]. For a HTML application, a POST action responds either with a page (in which case [@HttpCode(200)] is added) or with a redirect (see Example 20).

docs.title: 3.6. Example 12: Custom pipes and decorators
docs.text: You can write your own pipes and parameter decorators. The case study makes moderate use of them, but understanding them helps in understanding those of [NestJS].

docs.title: 3.6.1. A pipe: DateFrPipe
docs.text:
The file [src/date-fr.pipe.ts]:

import { BadRequestException, Injectable, PipeTransform } from '@nestjs/common';

// converts a French date "23/09/2026" to a ISO date "2026-09-23"
@Injectable()
export class DateFrPipe implements PipeTransform<string, string> {
  transform(valeur: string): string {
    const m = /^(\d{2})\/(\d{2})\/(\d{4})$/.exec(valeur ?? '');
    if (!m) {
      throw new BadRequestException(`[${valeur}] n'est pas une date au format jj/mm/aaaa`);
    }
    const [, jour, mois, annee] = m;
    const iso = `${annee}-${mois}-${jour}`;
     // "31/02/2026" is in the correct format, but does not exist
    if (new Date(`${iso}T00:00:00Z`).toISOString().slice(0, 10) !== iso) {
      throw new BadRequestException(`la date [${valeur}] n'existe pas`);
    }
    return iso;
  }
}
  • lines 4–5: a pipe is a class [@Injectable()] that implements the interface [PipeTransform<entrée, sortie>];
  • line 6: its method [transform] receives the parameter value and returns the transformed value, which will be received by the action;
  • lines 7–9: a value that does not have the form [jj/mm/aaaa] triggers a [BadRequestException] (400);
  • lines 13–15: a date that is in the correct format but does not exist (02/31/2026) is also rejected: [new Date] “corrects” it to 03/03/2026, which is detected.

docs.title: 3.6.2. A parameter decorator: @Language()
docs.text:
The file [src/langue.decorator.ts]:

import { createParamDecorator, ExecutionContext } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request } from 'express';

// @Language(): the browser’s preferred language, read from the header
// "Accept-Language: fr-FR,fr;q=0.9,en;q=0.8" -> "fr"
export const Langue = createParamDecorator((defaut: string | undefined, ctx: ExecutionContext): string => {
  const req = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request>();
  const entete = req.get('accept-language') ?? '';
  const premiere = entete.split(',')[0].trim().slice(0, 2).toLowerCase();
  return premiere || defaut || 'fr';
});
  • Line 6: [createParamDecorator] creates a parameter decorator, similar to [@Query] or [@Body]. The function receives the decorator’s argument ([@Langue('fr')]) and the query’s execution context;
  • line 7: the context provides access to the request [Express];
  • lines 8–10: the first two letters of the header [Accept-Language] are returned, which indicate the user’s preferred languages.

docs.title: 3.6.3. The controller
docs.text:
The file [src/exemples.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Query } from '@nestjs/common';
import { DateFrPipe } from './date-fr.pipe';
import { Langue } from './langue.decorator';
import { RechercheDto } from './recherche.dto';

@Controller('exemples')
export class ExemplesController {
   // /examples/calendar?day=23/09/2026: a custom pipe
  @Get('agenda')
  agenda(@Query('jour', DateFrPipe) jour: string): string {
    return `agenda du jour [${jour}]`;
  }

   // /examples/hello: a custom parameter decorator
  @Get('bonjour')
  bonjour(@Langue('fr') langue: string): string {
    return langue === 'en' ? 'Hello!' : 'Bonjour !';
  }

   // /examples/search?motCle=nest&admin=true: [admin] is not declared
  @Get('recherche')
  recherche(@Query() recherche: RechercheDto): object {
    return recherche;
  }
}
  • line 10: the pipe is used as [ParseIntPipe];
  • line 16: the decorator is used as [@Query];
  • Line 22: a template described by a class, this time using the [forbidNonWhitelisted] option from [ValidationPipe] (file [main.ts] below).

The [src/main.ts] file:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { ValidationPipe } from '@nestjs/common';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
  app.useGlobalPipes(
    new ValidationPipe({
      transform: true,
      whitelist: true, // undeclared fields are removed...
      forbidNonWhitelisted: true, // ... or, with this option, rejected (400)
    }),
  );
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Serveur démarré sur http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();

Line 11: With [forbidNonWhitelisted: true], an undeclared parameter in the class is no longer silently suppressed; it causes a 400 error.

The results:

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/exemples/agenda?jour=23/09/2026"

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 27

agenda du jour [2026-09-23]

curl -i "http://localhost:3000/exemples/agenda?jour=2026-09-23"

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 105

{"message":"[2026-09-23] n'est pas une date au format jj/mm/aaaa","error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}

docs.title: 3.6.4. Conclusion
docs.text: The action template is generated by [NestJS] based on the request: route parameters ([@Param]), URL ([@Query]), the body ([@Body]), and headers ([@Headers]). The pipes convert and validate these values. For a HTML application, it is usually preferable to validate the model yourself (example 09) so that you can redisplay the form. This is the subject of the next chapter.

docs.title: 7. The Lifecycle of a Request
docs.text:
Between the arrival of a request and the execution of the action, [NestJS] involves several types of objects, each with a specific role. We’ve already encountered some of them: middleware ([res.locals], [cookie-parser]) and pipes ([ParseIntPipe], [ValidationPipe]). The case study uses all five:

ObjectRoleIn the case studymiddlewareprepare the request; does not yet know the actionreading cookies, language, flash messagestoresauthorize or deny access to the actionAuthentication (JWT), rolesinterceptorcode before and after the actionthe logged-in user, exposed to viewspipeconvert and validate a parameter[ParseIntPipe]exception filterConvert an exception into a responseError pages HTML, redirection to /login

docs.title: 7.1. Example 24: The Five Steps
docs.text:
Example 24 has an action that calculates the square of a number and one object of each type. Each writes a line to the console, so we can see the order in which they occur.

The file [src/journal.middleware.ts]:

import { Injectable, NestMiddleware } from '@nestjs/common';
import { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';

// 1. MIDDLEWARE: the first to receive the request. It does not yet know
//     what action will process it
@Injectable()
export class JournalMiddleware implements NestMiddleware {
  use(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
    console.log(`\n--- ${req.method} ${req.originalUrl}`);
    console.log('1. middleware');
    next(); // control is passed to the next node in the chain
  }
}
  • Line 7: a middleware [NestJS] is a class that implements [NestMiddleware]. A simple function, as in the previous examples, would also work;
  • Line 11: The middleware must call [next()] to pass control to the next step (or send a response itself). Otherwise, the request remains blocked.

The file [src/app.module.ts]:

import { MiddlewareConsumer, Module, NestModule } from '@nestjs/common';
import { CalculController } from './calcul.controller';
import { JournalMiddleware } from './journal.middleware';

@Module({
  controllers: [CalculController],
})
export class AppModule implements NestModule {
   // A class-based middleware registers itself in the module
  configure(consumer: MiddlewareConsumer): void {
    consumer.apply(JournalMiddleware).forRoutes('*');
  }
}

Lines 10–12: A class-based middleware registers itself in a module that implements [NestModule]. [forRoutes('*')] applies it to all routes.

The file [src/bloquer.guard.ts]:

import { CanActivate, ExecutionContext, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request } from 'express';

// 2. GARDE: determines whether the request is authorized to reach the action.
//     false -> NestJS raises a ForbiddenException (403)
@Injectable()
export class BloquerGuard implements CanActivate {
  canActivate(contexte: ExecutionContext): boolean {
    const req = contexte.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request>();
     // the guard knows the target action (which the middleware did not know)
    console.log(`2. garde (action visée : ${contexte.getHandler().name})`);
    return req.query.bloquer !== '1';
  }
}
  • line 7: a guard implements [CanActivate];
  • line 8: its method [canActivate] receives the execution context and returns [true] (the request continues) or [false] ([NestJS] raises a [ForbiddenException], code 403);
  • line 11: unlike the middleware, the guard knows the target action ([getHandler()]) and its controller ([getClass()]). This is what allows a guard to read the decorators applied to the action (see [@Roles], next chapter).

The file [src/chrono.interceptor.ts]:

import { CallHandler, ExecutionContext, Injectable, NestInterceptor } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Observable, tap } from 'rxjs';

// 3. INTERCEPTEUR: from the code AVANT, the action, and APRÈS, it
@Injectable()
export class ChronoInterceptor implements NestInterceptor {
  intercept(contexte: ExecutionContext, suite: CallHandler): Observable<unknown> {
    console.log('3. intercepteur (avant)');
    const debut = Date.now();
     // suite.handle() executes the sequence: pipes followed by the action. The result
     // of the action arrives in the stream (Observable) returned
    return suite.handle().pipe(tap(() => console.log(`6. intercepteur (après, ${Date.now() - debut} ms)`)));
  }
}
  • line 6: an interceptor implements [NestInterceptor];
  • line 8: the code placed before [suite.handle()] executes before the action;
  • line 12: [suite.handle()] executes the rest (pipes followed by the action) and returns a stream [RxJS] ([Observable]) that will produce the result of the action. The [tap] operator executes code after the action, without modifying its result (the [map] operator would allow it to be modified).

The file [src/entier.pipe.ts]:

import { BadRequestException, Injectable, PipeTransform } from '@nestjs/common';

// 4. PIPE: converts and validates an action parameter
@Injectable()
export class EntierPipe implements PipeTransform<string, number> {
  transform(valeur: string): number {
    console.log(`4. pipe (valeur reçue : "${valeur}")`);
    const n = Number(valeur);
    if (!Number.isInteger(n)) {
      throw new BadRequestException(`"${valeur}" n'est pas un nombre entier`);
    }
    return n;
  }
}

A pipe similar to [ParseIntPipe] (see Example 12).

The file [src/page-erreur.filter.ts]:

import { ArgumentsHost, Catch, ExceptionFilter, HttpException, HttpStatus } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Response } from 'express';

// x. The FILTRE from EXCEPTIONS: receives any unhandled exceptions, regardless of
//     regardless of where it comes from (guard, pipe, action...), and generates the response.
//     @Catch() without arguments: all exceptions
@Catch()
export class PageErreurFilter implements ExceptionFilter {
  catch(exception: unknown, host: ArgumentsHost): void {
    const res = host.switchToHttp().getResponse<Response>();
    const status = exception instanceof HttpException ? exception.getStatus() : HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;
    const message = exception instanceof HttpException ? exception.message : 'Erreur interne';
    console.log(`x. filtre d'exceptions (${status} : ${message})`);
     // a page HTML rather than the default response JSON from NestJS
    res.status(status).render('erreur', { status, message });
  }
}
  • Line 7: [@Catch()] without an argument: the filter receives all exceptions. [@Catch(HttpException)] would limit it to the exceptions in HTTP;
  • Line 9: The [catch] method receives the exception and a [host] object that provides access to the request and the response;
  • Line 11: A [HttpException] contains its status code. Any other exception (a programming error, an unreachable database) results in a 500 error;
  • line 15: instead of the default JSON, the filter displays a HTML page with the correct status code.

The file [src/main.ts]:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { NestExpressApplication } from '@nestjs/platform-express';
import { dirname, join } from 'path';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';
import { ChronoInterceptor } from './chrono.interceptor';
import { PageErreurFilter } from './page-erreur.filter';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule, { logger: ['error', 'warn'] });
  app.useStaticAssets(join(dirname(require.resolve('bootstrap/package.json')), 'dist'), { prefix: '/bootstrap/' });
  app.setBaseViewsDir(join(__dirname, '..', 'views'));
  app.setViewEngine('hbs');
   // an interceptor and a filter GLOBAUX: they apply to all routes
  app.useGlobalInterceptors(new ChronoInterceptor());
  app.useGlobalFilters(new PageErreurFilter());
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Serveur démarré sur http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();
  • line 9: we filter the messages from [NestJS] down to errors and warnings, so we can see our own more clearly;
  • lines 14–15: the interceptor and filter are global; they apply to all actions.

The file [src/calcul.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Param, Render, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
import { BloquerGuard } from './bloquer.guard';
import { EntierPipe } from './entier.pipe';

@Controller('carre')
@UseGuards(BloquerGuard) // the guard applies to all controller actions
export class CalculController {
  @Get(':n')
  @Render('carre')
  carre(@Param('n', EntierPipe) n: number): object {
    console.log(`5. action carre(${n})`);
    if (n === 13) {
      throw new Error('13 porte malheur'); // an "unexpected" error
    }
    return { n, carre: n * n };
  }
}
  • line 6: [@UseGuards] applies a guard to all controller actions (it can also be applied to a single action);
  • line 10: the pipe converts the parameter;
  • lines 12–14: an “unexpected” error, to see the filter in action.

Four requests: a normal calculation, an invalid parameter, a request blocked by the guard, and the unexpected error. The server console:

--- GET /carre/7
1. middleware
2. garde (action visée : carre)
3. intercepteur (avant)
4. pipe (valeur reçue : "7")
5. action carre(7)
6. intercepteur (après, 2 ms)

--- GET /carre/abc
1. middleware
2. garde (action visée : carre)
3. intercepteur (avant)
4. pipe (valeur reçue : "abc")
x. filtre d'exceptions (400 : "abc" n'est pas un nombre entier)

--- GET /carre/7?bloquer=1
1. middleware
2. garde (action visée : carre)
x. filtre d'exceptions (403 : Forbidden resource)

--- GET /carre/13
1. middleware
2. garde (action visée : carre)
3. intercepteur (avant)
4. pipe (valeur reçue : "13")
5. action carre(13)
x. filtre d'exceptions (500 : Erreur interne)

This log shows:

  • the order of the steps: middleware, guard, interceptor (before), pipe, action, interceptor (after);
  • an exception interrupts the chain, wherever it occurs, and the filter generates the response: the guard denies access (403), the pipe denies access (400), the action fails (500).

The resulting pages:

The exception filter in the case study ([web/html-exception.filter.ts]) follows this pattern, with one exception: a 401 error (user not logged in) does not display an error page but redirects to the login page.

docs.title: 4. The View and Its Model
docs.text: Up to this point, actions have generated their own responses. In a MVC application, this is the role of a view: a file that describes the page HTML, with placeholders for the data passed to it by the action—the view’s model. We will use the [Handlebars] view engine via the [hbs] package, which adapts it to [Express].

docs.title: 4.1. Example 13: A First View
docs.text:
13-premiere-vue/
├── src/
│   ├── app.module.ts
│   ├── main.ts
│   └── vues.controller.ts
├── views/
│   ├── inconnu.hbs
│   └── index.hbs
├── nest-cli.json
└── tsconfig.json

The [src/main.ts] file:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { NestExpressApplication } from '@nestjs/platform-express';
import { join } from 'path';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

async function bootstrap() {
   // NestExpressApplication: provides access to Express-specific methods
  const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule);
   // the views are in the [views] folder, at the root of the project;
   // Once compiled, this file is located in `dist/`: the root is therefore `'..'`
  app.setBaseViewsDir(join(__dirname, '..', 'views'));
   // the view engine: Handlebars, provided by the [hbs] package
  app.setViewEngine('hbs');
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Serveur démarré sur http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();

Let’s break down this code:

  • Line 2: [NestExpressApplication] is the type of an application [NestJS] that relies on [Express] ([NestJS] can also use the [Fastify] server). Specifying this provides access to the methods specific to [Express]: [setBaseViewsDir], [setViewEngine], [useStaticAssets];
  • line 8: the type is changed to [NestFactory.create];
  • Line 11: the views folder. [__dirname] is the folder for the currently running file: [dist], since [dist/main.js] is currently running. The [views] folder is therefore in [dist/../views];
  • line 13: the view engine: [hbs]. The views are the [.hbs] files in the views folder.

The file [src/vues.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Param, Render, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Response } from 'express';

@Controller()
export class VuesController {
   // @Render('index'): the object rendered by the action is the MODÈLE from the view
   // views/index.hbs; NestJS itself calls the view engine
  @Get()
  @Render('index')
  accueil(): object {
    return {
      titre: 'Ma première vue',
      message: 'Cette page a été fabriquée par Handlebars, sur le serveur.',
      heure: new Date().toLocaleTimeString('fr-FR'),
    };
  }

   // res.render(view, template): the view is selected PENDANT when the action is executed
  @Get('bonjour/:nom')
  bonjour(@Param('nom') nom: string, @Res() res: Response): void {
    if (nom === 'inconnu') {
      res.status(404).render('inconnu', { nom });
      return;
    }
    res.render('index', {
      titre: `Bonjour ${nom}`,
      message: 'Cette fois, la vue a été choisie par res.render.',
      heure: new Date().toLocaleTimeString('fr-FR'),
    });
  }
}
  • lines 8–9: [@Render('index')] refers to the view [views/index.hbs]. The object returned by the action is no longer the response; it is the view template;
  • lines 11–15: the template: three values, [titre], [message], and [heure];
  • lines 19–30: When the view depends on the request, the action uses [res.render(vue, modèle)] from the response [Express] (injected by [@Res()]; see Example 05). Here, the name [inconnu] displays another view, with status code 404.

The file [views/index.hbs]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>{{titre}}</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>{{titre}}</h1>
  <p>{{message}}</p>
  <p>Page fabriquée à {{heure}}.</p>
</body>
</html>

A view named [Handlebars] is a file named HTML. Each instance of [{{titre}}] (lines 5, 8) is replaced by the value of the corresponding field in the template. The result:

The source code of the page received by the browser no longer contains any trace of [Handlebars]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Ma première vue</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Ma première vue</h1>
  <p>Cette page a été fabriquée par Handlebars, sur le serveur.</p>
  <p>Page fabriquée à 16:10:29.</p>
</body>
</html>

URL and [/bonjour/martin] display the same view using a different template:

and [/bonjour/inconnu] displays yet another view:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/hello/unknown

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 168

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Inconnu</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Personne ne s'appelle [inconnu] ici</h1>
</body>
</html>

docs.title: 4.2. Example 14: The Handlebars language
docs.text:
[Handlebars] is a template language without logic: a view contains no [JavaScript] code, only [{{...}}] expressions and a few blocks ([{{#if}}], [{{#each}}]...). All calculations are performed beforehand by the action. Example 14 demonstrates this. The template:

The [src/bases.controller.ts] file:

import { Controller, Get, Render } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller()
export class BasesController {
  @Get()
  @Render('bases')
  bases(): object {
    return {
      titre: 'Les bases de Handlebars',
      nom: 'Martin',
      html: '<b>ceci est du HTML</b>',
      connecte: true,
      devise: '€',
      produits: [
        { nom: 'Clavier', prix: 25, enStock: true },
        { nom: 'Souris', prix: 12.5, enStock: false },
        { nom: 'Écran', prix: 149, enStock: true },
      ],
      panier: [],
      adresse: { rue: '12 rue des Lilas', ville: 'Angers' },
    };
  }
}

The view:

The file [views/bases.hbs]:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>{{titre}}</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>{{titre}}</h1>
  {{!-- 1. afficher une valeur du modèle --}}
  <p>1. Nom : {{nom}} - variable absente : [{{inexistante}}]</p>
  {{!-- 2. {{ }} échappe le HTML, {{{ }}} l'insère tel quel --}}
  <p>2a. {{html}}</p>
  <p>2b. {{{html}}}</p>
  {{!-- 3. une condition --}}
  {{#if logged in}}
    <p>3. Vous êtes connecté.</p>
  {{else}}
    <p>3. Vous n'êtes pas connecté.</p>
  {{/if}}
  {{#unless connected}}
    <p>Ce paragraphe n'est pas affiché.</p>
  {{/unless}}
  {{!-- 4. une boucle ; dans la boucle, le contexte est l'élément courant --}}
  <p>4. Nos produits :</p>
  <ul>
    {{#each product}}
      <li>n° {{@index}} : {{nom}}, {{prix}} {{../devise}}
        {{#if enStock}}(in stock){{else}}(out of stock){{/if}}
        {{#if @first}}- the first{{/if}}
        {{#if @last}}- the last one, as seen by {{@root.nom}}{{/if}}
      </li>
    {{/each}}
  </ul>
  {{!-- 5. {{else}} dans une boucle : le cas de la liste vide --}}
  <p>5. Votre panier :
    {{#each shopping cart}}{{name}}{{else}}it is empty.{{/each}}
  </p>
  {{!-- 6. changer de contexte, ou utiliser un chemin pointé --}}
  {{#with address}}
    <p>6a. Adresse : {{rue}}, {{ville}}</p>
  {{/with}}
  <p>6b. Ville : {{adresse.ville}}</p>
</body>
</html>

Let's comment on this code:

  • Line 9: [{{!-- ... --}}] is a comment ([Handlebars]): it does not appear on the generated page (unlike a comment such as HTML or [<!-- -->]);
  • line 10: a variable missing from the template ([inexistante]) produces an empty string, without an error;
  • lines 12–13: [{{html}}] escapes the special characters in HTML ([<] becomes [<]...): the text is displayed as-is. [{{{{{{html}}}}}}] (three curly braces) is inserted without escaping: it is interpreted as HTML. Triple curly braces are used only for HTML generated by the application, never for user-entered data: a user could inject HTML, or even [JavaScript], into the page (a so-called [XSS] attack);
  • lines 15–19: [{{#if}}] / [{{else}}] / [{{/if}}]: a conditional block. The condition is a value from the template, not an expression: [false], [undefined], [null], [''], [0], and the empty array are false;
  • lines 20–22: [{{#unless}}] is the inverse of [{{#if}}];
  • Lines 26–32: [{{#each}}] repeats its content for each element in an array. Within the block, the context is the current element: [{{{{nom}}}}] is the name of the current product. Special variables are available: [@index] (position starting at 0), [@first], [@last]. [../devise] points to the parent context, [@root.nom] to the root model;
  • line 36: a [{{else}}] within a [{{#each}}] handles the case of an empty array;
  • Lines 39–41: [{{#with}}] changes context; a relative path can also be used (line 42).

The code HTML produces:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Les bases de Handlebars</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Les bases de Handlebars</h1>
  <p>1. Nom : Martin - variable absente : []</p>
  <p>2a. <b>ceci est du HTML</b></p>
  <p>2b. <b>ceci est du HTML</b></p>
    <p>3. Vous êtes connecté.</p>
  <p>4. Nos produits :</p>
  <ul>
      <li>n° 0 : Clavier, 25 €
        (en stock)
        - le premier

      </li>
      <li>n° 1 : Souris, 12.5 €
        (épuisé)


      </li>
      <li>n° 2 : Écran, 149 €
        (en stock)

        - le dernier, vu par Martin
      </li>
  </ul>
  <p>5. Votre panier :
    il est vide.
  </p>
    <p>6a. Adresse : 12 rue des Lilas, Angers</p>
  <p>6b. Ville : Angers</p>
</body>
</html>

Note the blank lines left by the blocks: they have no effect on the display.

docs.title: 4.3. Example 15: Template, Partials, Static Files
docs.text:
The pages of a site share a common template (header, navigation bar, footer). [hbs] handles this as follows: if the views folder contains a file named [layout.hbs], every view is inserted into this template. Reusable page fragments are called partial views.

15-layout-partiels/
├── public/
│   └── css/
│       └── styles.css
├── src/
│   ├── app.module.ts
│   ├── main.ts
│   └── pages.controller.ts
├── views/
│   ├── partials/
│   │   ├── carte.hbs
│   │   └── navbar.hbs
│   ├── accueil.hbs
│   ├── brute.hbs
│   ├── equipe.hbs
│   └── layout.hbs
├── nest-cli.json
└── tsconfig.json

The file [src/main.ts]:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { NestExpressApplication } from '@nestjs/platform-express';
import { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import * as hbs from 'hbs';
import { dirname, join } from 'path';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';

const RACINE = join(__dirname, '..');

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule);

   // 1. Static files: public/css/styles.css is served from /css/styles.css
  app.useStaticAssets(join(RACINE, 'public'));
   // Bootstrap is served directly from node_modules, under /bootstrap/
  app.useStaticAssets(join(dirname(require.resolve('bootstrap/package.json')), 'dist'), { prefix: '/bootstrap/' });

   // 2. Views: views/layout.hbs will be the template for the pages at TOUTES
  app.setBaseViewsDir(join(RACINE, 'views'));
  app.setViewEngine('hbs');
   // 3. Partials: views/partials/xxx.hbs is inserted via {{> xxx}}
  await new Promise<void>((fini) => hbs.registerPartials(join(RACINE, 'views', 'partials'), () => fini()));

   // 4. An Express middleware: what it inserts into res.locals is
   /   / added to the CHAQUE view template
  app.use((req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
    res.locals.chemin = req.path;
    res.locals.annee = new Date().getFullYear();
    next();
  });

  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Serveur démarré sur http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();

Let’s break down this code:

  • line 14: [useStaticAssets] serves static files from a folder: the file [public/css/styles.css] is served to URL and [/css/styles.css] as-is, without going through a controller;
  • line 16: the CSS [Bootstrap] framework is served directly from the [node_modules] folder, under the prefix [/bootstrap/]. [require.resolve] locates the [bootstrap] package folder, wherever it is installed (here in [exemples/node_modules]);
  • line 22: the files in the [views/partials] folder become partial files: [partials/navbar.hbs] is inserted into a view by [{{> navbar}}]. [registerPartials] reads the folder asynchronously: we wait for it to finish (the function passed as the second argument is called at the end) before starting the server;
  • Lines 26–30: a [Express] middleware, executed before each request. What it stores in [res.locals] is added to the template of each view. This is how we provide common information (in this case, the requested path and the year) to all pages without repeating it in every action.

The [views/layout.hbs] file:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>{{titre}} - Mon site</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-3">
    {{> navbar}}
    {{!-- la vue demandée par l'action est insérée ici --}}
    {{{body}}}
    <footer class="pied">Page [{{chemin}}] - © {{annee}}</footer>
  </div>
</body>
</html>
  • lines 7–8: the style sheets, served by [useStaticAssets];
  • line 12: insertion of the partial [navbar];
  • line 14: [{{{body}}}] is the location where [hbs] inserts the view requested by the action. Triple curly braces: the view comes from the pre-generated HTML and must not be escaped;
  • line 15: [chemin] and [annee] come from [res.locals] (the middleware for [main.ts]).

The file [views/partials/navbar.hbs]:

The [carte] partial displays a name and a job title. It is used in two ways:

The [views/accueil.hbs] file:

<h1>Bienvenue</h1>
<p>Cette page ne contient que son propre contenu : l'entête, la barre de
  navigation et le pied de page viennent du gabarit <code>layout.hbs</code>.</p>
{{> carte nom="Un partiel" fonction="inséré avec des paramètres nommés"}}

line 4: with named parameters: the partial receives them as context;

The [views/equipe.hbs] file:

<h1>{{titre}}</h1>
<div class="row g-3">
  {{#each members}}
    <div class="col-md-4">
      {{!-- sans paramètre, le partiel reçoit le contexte courant : le membre --}}
      {{> carte}}

line 6: no parameters: the partial receives the current context, in this case the current team member in the loop [{{#each}}].

The file [src/pages.controller.ts]:

import { Controller, Get, Render } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller()
export class PagesController {
  @Get()
  @Render('accueil')
  accueil(): object {
    return { titre: 'Accueil' };
  }

  @Get('equipe')
  @Render('equipe')
  equipe(): object {
    return {
      titre: 'Notre équipe',
      membres: [
        { nom: 'Marie Pélissier', fonction: 'Directrice' },
        { nom: 'Jacques Bromard', fonction: 'Développeur' },
        { nom: 'Philippe Jandot', fonction: 'Graphiste' },
      ],
    };
  }

   // layout: false: the view is rendered as SEULE, without the common template
  @Get('brute')
  @Render('brute')
  brute(): object {
    return { layout: false };
  }
}

Lines 25–29: The [layout: false] field in the model instructs [hbs] not to use the template: the [brute.hbs] view is a complete HTML page. We could also specify a different template ([layout: 'autre']). The resulting pages:

The template, the partial views, and [res.locals] are exactly what the case study uses: a view ([layout.hbs]), partial views for the navigation bar, messages, and confirmation windows, and middleware that prepares the language and the message to be displayed.

docs.title: 4.4. Example 16: Helpers
docs.text:
A helper is a [TypeScript] function that can be called from a view. It compensates for the lack of logic in [Handlebars]: comparing two values, formatting a date or a price, translating text... The blocks [{{#if}}] and [{{#each}}] are themselves predefined helpers.

The [src/helpers.ts] file:

import { HelperOptions } from 'handlebars';

// the 'hbs' module has no type declarations: we describe which ones we use
interface Hbs {
  registerHelper(nom: string, fonction: (...args: any[]) => unknown): void;
  handlebars: { SafeString: new (html: string) => unknown; escapeExpression(texte: string): string };
}

export function enregistrerHelpers(hbs: Hbs): void {
   // {{capitalized name}}: a simple helper, one argument
  hbs.registerHelper('majuscules', (texte: unknown) => String(texte ?? '').toUpperCase());

   // {{#if (eq a b)}}: used as a sub-expression, enclosed in parentheses
  hbs.registerHelper('eq', (a: unknown, b: unknown) => a === b);

   // {{active path '/products'}}: "active" if the current page is under this path
  hbs.registerHelper('actif', (chemin: unknown, prefixe: unknown) =>
    typeof chemin === 'string' && typeof prefixe === 'string' && chemin.startsWith(prefixe) ? 'active' : '',
  );

   // {{currency amount currency='USD'}}: the DERNIER argument of a helper is always
   // the Handlebars object [options]; options.hash contains the parameters
   // named parameters, and options.data.root the complete page template (including res.locals)
  hbs.registerHelper('monnaie', (montant: unknown, options: HelperOptions) => {
    const devise = options.hash.devise ?? 'EUR';
    const langue = options.data?.root?.lang ?? 'fr-FR';
    return new Intl.NumberFormat(langue, { style: 'currency', currency: devise }).format(Number(montant));
  });

   // {{date when}}: a date in the format of the page's language
  hbs.registerHelper('date', (quand: unknown, options: HelperOptions) => {
    const langue = options.data?.root?.lang ?? 'fr-FR';
    return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(langue, { dateStyle: 'full' }).format(new Date(String(quand)));
  });

   // {{stock badge}}: a helper that generates HTML. SafeString indicates to
   // Handlebars not to PAS escape it; it is then up to the helper to escape
   // the data it inserts (escapeExpression)
  hbs.registerHelper('badge', (stock: unknown) => {
    const n = Number(stock);
    const classe = n > 0 ? 'text-bg-success' : 'text-bg-danger';
    const texte = hbs.handlebars.escapeExpression(n > 0 ? `${n} en stock` : 'épuisé');
    return new hbs.handlebars.SafeString(`<span class="badge ${classe}">${texte}</span>`);
  });
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 4–7: the [hbs] package has no type declarations [TypeScript]: we describe which ones we use;
  • line 11: [hbs.registerHelper(nom, fonction)] defines a helper. In a view, [{{majuscules nom}}] calls the function with the value of [nom];
  • line 14: [eq] returns a Boolean. It is used as a sub-expression, enclosed in parentheses, within another helper: [{{#if (eq chemin '/')}}];
  • lines 17–19: [actif] returns the class CSS [active] if the page path begins with a given prefix;
  • lines 24–28: The last argument of a helper is always an object provided by [Handlebars] or [options]. [options.hash] contains the named parameters ([{{monnaie prix devise='USD'}}]), and [options.data.root] contains the root template of the page, to which [res.locals] has been added. The helper retrieves the page's language from there, even if it is called from within a [{{#each}}]. Formatting is handled by the standard object [Intl.NumberFormat];
  • lines 31–34: same principle applies to a date, using [Intl.DateTimeFormat];
  • Lines 39–44: A helper that generates HTML. By default, the output of a helper is escaped, just like any [{{...}}] expression. To avoid this, it is returned in the form of [SafeString]. The helper must then escape the data it inserts into its HTML ([escapeExpression]) itself.

The [src/main.ts] file:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { NestExpressApplication } from '@nestjs/platform-express';
import { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import * as hbs from 'hbs';
import { dirname, join } from 'path';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';
import { enregistrerHelpers } from './helpers';

const RACINE = join(__dirname, '..');

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule);
  app.useStaticAssets(join(RACINE, 'public'));
  app.useStaticAssets(join(dirname(require.resolve('bootstrap/package.json')), 'dist'), { prefix: '/bootstrap/' });
  app.setBaseViewsDir(join(RACINE, 'views'));
  app.setViewEngine('hbs');
   // Helpers: functions TypeScript that can be called from views
  enregistrerHelpers(hbs);
  await new Promise<void>((fini) => hbs.registerPartials(join(RACINE, 'views', 'partials'), () => fini()));
  app.use((req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
    res.locals.chemin = req.path;
    res.locals.lang = req.query.lang === 'en' ? 'en-US' : 'fr-FR';
    next();
  });
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Serveur démarré sur http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();
  • line 18: helpers are registered at startup;
  • line 22: the middleware selects the formatting language based on the [lang] parameter in URL (a simple way to test; the next chapter will explain it better).

The [views/partials/navbar.hbs] file:

<nav class="navbar navbar-expand bg-light rounded mb-3 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand">Helpers</span>
  <div class="navbar-nav">
    {{!-- le lien de la page courante reçoit la classe "active" --}}
    <a class="nav-link {{#if (eq chemin '/')}}active{{/if}}" href="/">Accueil</a>
    <a class="nav-link {{actif chemin '/produits'}}" href="/produits">Produits</a>
  </div>
</nav>

Lines 5–6: The two ways to highlight the link on the current page: [eq] as a sub-expression within a [{{#if}}], or the [actif] helper, which is more concise. The case study uses [actif].

The [views/produits.hbs] file:

<h1>{{titre}}</h1>
<table class="table table-sm w-auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Produit</th><th>Prix</th><th>Prix en dollars</th><th>Stock</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    {{#each products}}
      <tr>
        <td>{{majuscules nom}}</td>
        <td>{{monnaie prix}}</td>
        <td>{{monnaie prix devise='USD'}}</td>
        <td>{{badge stock}}</td>
      </tr>
    {{/each}}
  </tbody>
</table>

The resulting pages, first in French and then in English ([?lang=en]):

docs.title: 4.5. Example 17: A GET form
docs.text:
A HTML form sent using the GET method places its fields in the URL. This is the appropriate method for a search: it does not modify anything, and the resulting URL can be bookmarked or shared. The case study uses it to select a doctor and a date.

The [src/livres.controller.ts] file:

import { Controller, Get, Query, Render } from '@nestjs/common';

interface Livre {
  titre: string;
  auteur: string;
  genre: string;
}

const LIVRES: Livre[] = [
  { titre: 'Le Rouge et le Noir', auteur: 'Stendhal', genre: 'roman' },
  { titre: 'Les Fleurs du mal', auteur: 'Baudelaire', genre: 'poésie' },
  { titre: 'Madame Bovary', auteur: 'Flaubert', genre: 'roman' },
  { titre: 'Alcools', auteur: 'Apollinaire', genre: 'poésie' },
  { titre: 'Le Cid', auteur: 'Corneille', genre: 'théâtre' },
];
const GENRES = ['roman', 'poésie', 'théâtre'];

@Controller()
export class LivresController {
   // GET /search?motCle=...&genre=... : the ET form and its results
  @Get(['/', 'recherche'])
  @Render('recherche')
  recherche(@Query('motCle') motCle = '', @Query('genre') genre = ''): object {
    const mot = motCle.trim().toLowerCase();
    const resultats = LIVRES.filter(
      (l) =>
        (mot === '' || l.titre.toLowerCase().includes(mot) || l.auteur.toLowerCase().includes(mot)) &&
        (genre === '' || l.genre === genre),
    );
    return { motCle, genre, genres: GENRES, resultats, nombre: resultats.length };
  }
}
  • lines 9–15: the books, in memory;
  • line 21: an array of paths: the action processes [GET /] and [GET /recherche];
  • line 23: a default value, [TypeScript], replaces a missing parameter (on the first visit, the form has not yet been submitted);
  • lines 24–29: filtering;
  • line 30: the template contains the entered values ([motCle], [genre]); so that the form can display them again, along with the list of genres and the results.

The file [views/recherche.hbs]:

<h1 class="h3">Recherche de livres</h1>
{{!-- method="get" : les champs sont envoyés dans l'URL (?motCle=...&genre=...) --}}
<form method="get" action="/recherche" class="row g-2 align-items-end mb-3">
  <div class="col-auto">
    <label class="form-label" for="motCle">Titre ou auteur</label>
    {{!-- value="{{motCle}}" : le champ réaffiche ce qui a été saisi --}}
    <input class="form-control" id="motCle" name="motCle" value="{{motCle}}">
  </div>
  <div class="col-auto">
    <label class="form-label" for="genre">Genre</label>
    <select class="form-select" id="genre" name="genre">
      <option value="">(tous)</option>
      {{#each genres}}
        <option value="{{this}}" {{#if (eq this ../genre)}}selected{{/if}}>{{this}}</option>
      {{/each}}
    </select>
  </div>
  <div class="col-auto">
    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Rechercher</button>
  </div>
</form>
<p>{{nombre}} livre(s) trouvé(s).</p>
<ul>
  {{#each results}}
    <li><i>{{titre}}</i>, {{auteur}} ({{genre}})</li>
  {{/each}}
</ul>
  • Line 3: [method="get"] and [action="/recherche"]: Submitting the form is a [GET /recherche?motCle=...&genre=...] request. The parameter names are the [name] attribute of each field;
  • Line 7: The [value] attribute redisplays the entry;
  • lines 13–15: In the drop-down list, the option matching the selected category is assigned the attribute [selected]. In the loop, [this] is the current element (a string) and [../genre] is the type of the parent model.

Upon initial display, and then after a search:

The address bar shows the parameters that were sent. Accented characters and spaces are encoded there ([%C3%A9]...): this is the encoding URL, which [NestJS] decodes before populating [@Query].

docs.title: 4.6. Example 18: Form Fields
docs.text:
Example 18 includes all types of HTML fields: text, password, date, radio buttons, checkboxes, drop-down list, multi-select list, text box, and hidden field. It shows how the server receives them and how the view displays them.

The [src/listes.service.ts] file:

import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';

// the lists provided by the form. In a real application, they
// would come from a database: they would be read UNE times at startup,
// since they are the same for all users
@Injectable()
export class ListesService {
  readonly titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
  readonly pays = [
    { code: 'fr', nom: 'France' },
    { code: 'be', nom: 'Belgique' },
    { code: 'ch', nom: 'Suisse' },
    { code: 'ca', nom: 'Canada' },
  ];
  readonly loisirs = ['lecture', 'musique', 'sport', 'cinéma'];
  readonly langues = ['français', 'anglais', 'espagnol', 'allemand'];
}

The lists offered by the form are provided by a service. They are the same for all users: a service, instantiated only once (application scope; see Chapter 6), is the natural place to store them.

The file [src/formulaire.controller.ts]:

import { Body, Controller, Get, HttpCode, Post, Render } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ListesService } from './listes.service';

// what the user entered, once formatted
interface Saisie {
  nom: string;
  motDePasse: string;
  commentaire: string;
  titre: string;
  loisirs: string[];
  pays: string;
  langues: string[];
  naissance: string;
  jeton: string;
}

@Controller('formulaire')
export class FormulaireController {
  constructor(private readonly listes: ListesService) {}

   // GET: the form, with initial values
  @Get()
  @Render('formulaire')
  afficher(): object {
    const initial: Saisie = {
      nom: '', motDePasse: '', commentaire: '', titre: 'Mme', loisirs: [],
      pays: 'fr', langues: ['français'], naissance: '', jeton: 'A7X2',
    };
    return this.modele(initial, null);
  }

   // POST: we receive the entered values and redisplay the form
  @Post()
  @HttpCode(200) // A POST response returns 201 by default; here, a page is returned
  @Render('formulaire')
  traiter(@Body() corps: Record<string, string | string[]>): object {
    const saisie: Saisie = {
      nom: texte(corps.nom),
      motDePasse: texte(corps.motDePasse),
      commentaire: texte(corps.commentaire),
      titre: texte(corps.titre),
      loisirs: tableau(corps.loisirs),
      pays: texte(corps.pays),
      langues: tableau(corps.langues),
      naissance: texte(corps.naissance),
      jeton: texte(corps.jeton),
    };
    return this.modele(saisie, corps);
  }

   // the view template: the lists, with each option checked
   // checked/selected based on the user’s input
  private modele(saisie: Saisie, recu: object | null): object {
    return {
      saisie,
      titres: this.listes.titres.map((t) => ({ valeur: t, coche: t === saisie.titre })),
      loisirs: this.listes.loisirs.map((l) => ({ valeur: l, coche: saisie.loisirs.includes(l) })),
      pays: this.listes.pays.map((p) => ({ ...p, selectionne: p.code === saisie.pays })),
      langues: this.listes.langues.map((l) => ({ valeur: l, selectionne: saisie.langues.includes(l) })),
      recu: recu ? JSON.stringify(recu, null, 2) : null,
    };
  }
}

// A missing field (unchecked box...) is not sent at all
function texte(valeur: unknown): string {
  return typeof valeur === 'string' ? valeur : '';
}

// one value checked: "sport"; two: ["sport", "musique"]; none: undefined
function tableau(valeur: unknown): string[] {
  if (valeur === undefined) return [];
  return Array.isArray(valeur) ? valeur : [String(valeur)];
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 5–15: data entry and formatting: the checkboxes and the drop-down list are arrays;
  • line 19: the list service is injected;
  • lines 22–30: [GET /formulaire] displays the form with initial values;
  • line 34: [POST /formulaire] returns a page, not a created resource: we replace the 201 code with 200;
  • lines 37–47: the received fields are reformatted. Two cases require attention: a missing field (an unchecked box is not sent at all, see function [texte], lines 66–68), and a multi-value field, which arrives as a string if it has only one value (function [tableau], lines 71–74, see Example 10);
  • lines 53–62: the view template. For each list, the action calculates which options should be checked or selected: the view then only needs to evaluate a Boolean. The field [recu] contains what the server received, for display purposes.

The file [views/formulaire.hbs]:

<h1 class="h3">Un formulaire complet</h1>
<form method="post" action="/formulaire" style="max-width: 40rem">
  {{!-- champ caché : envoyé avec le formulaire, mais invisible --}}
  <input type="hidden" name="jeton" value="{{saisie.jeton}}">

  <div class="mb-2">
    <span class="form-label me-3">Titre</span>
    {{#each titles}}
      {{!-- boutons radio : même [name], une seule valeur envoyée --}}
      <div class="form-check form-check-inline">
        <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="titre" id="titre-{{valeur}}"
               value="{{valeur}}" {{#if checked}}checked{{/if}}>
        <label class="form-check-label" for="titre-{{valeur}}">{{valeur}}</label>
      </div>
    {{/each}}
  </div>

  <div class="row g-2 mb-2">
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="nom">Nom</label>
      <input class="form-control" type="text" id="nom" name="nom" value="{{saisie.nom}}">
    </div>
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="motDePasse">Mot de passe</label>
      {{!-- un mot de passe n'est JAMAIS renvoyé dans la page --}}
      <input class="form-control" type="password" id="motDePasse" name="motDePasse">
    </div>
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="naissance">Date de naissance</label>
      <input class="form-control" type="date" id="naissance" name="naissance" value="{{saisie.naissance}}">
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="mb-2">
    <span class="form-label me-3">Loisirs</span>
    {{#each leisure}}
      {{!-- cases à cocher : même [name], plusieurs valeurs possibles --}}
      <div class="form-check form-check-inline">
        <input class="form-check-input" type="checkbox" name="loisirs" id="loisir-{{@index}}"
               value="{{valeur}}" {{#if checked}}checked{{/if}}>
        <label class="form-check-label" for="loisir-{{@index}}">{{valeur}}</label>
      </div>
    {{/each}}
  </div>

  <div class="row g-2 mb-2">
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="pays">Pays</label>
      <select class="form-select" id="pays" name="pays">
        {{#each country}}
          <option value="{{code}}" {{#if selected}}selected{{/if}}>{{name}}</option>
        {{/each}}
      </select>
    </div>
    <div class="col">
      <label class="form-label" for="langues">Langues parlées</label>
      {{!-- liste à sélection multiple : plusieurs valeurs possibles --}}
      <select class="form-select" id="langues" name="langues" multiple size="4">
        {{#each language}}
          <option value="{{valeur}}" {{#if selected}}selected{{/if}}>{{value}}</option>
        {{/each}}
      </select>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="mb-2">
    <label class="form-label" for="commentaire">Commentaire</label>
    {{!-- une zone de texte : la valeur est ENTRE les balises --}}
    <textarea class="form-control" id="commentaire" name="commentaire" rows="2">{{saisie.commentaire}}</textarea>
  </div>

  <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Envoyer</button>
</form>

{{#if received}}
  <h2 class="h5 mt-3">Ce que le serveur a reçu</h2>
  <pre class="bg-light p-2 border">{{recu}}</pre>
{{/if}}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • line 2: the form is submitted via POST; its fields are included in the request body;
  • line 4: a hidden field is sent with the form but is not displayed. It is used to pass information from one page to the next (the case study uses it, for example, to store the version of a record). Note: the user can modify it;
  • lines 8–15: radio buttons share the same [name] attribute: only one can be selected, and only one value is sent. The [checked] attribute selects the button;
  • line 26: a password is never sent back in a page: the field has no [value] attribute;
  • line 30: a date field. The browser displays the date in the user’s format, but always sends [aaaa-mm-jj];
  • lines 36–43: checkboxes with the same [name] attribute: each checked box sends its value; the parameter is therefore repeated;
  • lines 49–53: a drop-down list. The selected option has the attribute [selected];
  • lines 58–62: the [multiple] attribute allows you to select multiple options;
  • line 69: the value of a text field is enclosed within its tags, not in a [value] attribute;
  • Lines 75–78: What the server received, displayed within a [<pre>] tag.

The initial form, then after submission:

Note that the text box redisplayed [Bonjour <b>tout</b> le monde] exactly as entered: thanks to the escaping of [{{...}}], the entered tags are not interpreted. The password was received but is not displayed. With [curl], we can see the difference when a checkbox is selected:

curl -d "jeton=A7X2&titre=Mr&nom=Martin&loisirs=sport" http://localhost:3000/form

{
  "jeton": "A7X2",
  "titre": "Mr",
  "nom": "Martin",
  "loisirs": "sport"
}

and two checked boxes:

curl -d "jeton=A7X2&titre=Mr&nom=Martin&loisirs=sport&loisirs=musique" http://localhost:3000/form

{
  "jeton": "A7X2",
  "titre": "Mr",
  "nom": "Martin",
  "loisirs": [
    "sport",
    "musique"
  ]
}

(only the [Ce que le serveur a reçu] section of the page is shown)

docs.title: 4.7. Example 19: Form Validation
docs.text:
An invalid form must be redisplayed, showing the entered values and a message below each field with an error. Example 19 applies the technique from Example 09 (validation performed by the action) to a registration form.

The file [src/inscription.dto.ts]:

import { Transform, Type } from 'class-transformer';
import { IsEmail, IsInt, IsNotEmpty, Max, MaxLength, Min, MinLength } from 'class-validator';

// removes unnecessary spaces from an entry AVANT upon validation
const nettoyer = ({ value }: { value: unknown }) => (typeof value === 'string' ? value.trim() : value);

export class InscriptionDto {
  @Transform(nettoyer)
  @IsNotEmpty({ message: 'Le nom est obligatoire.' })
  @MaxLength(20, { message: 'Le nom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.' })
  nom: string;

  @Transform(nettoyer)
  @IsEmail({}, { message: 'Adresse électronique invalide.' })
  email: string;

   // Everything from a form is a string: "42" -> 42
  @Type(() => Number)
  @IsInt({ message: "L'âge doit être un nombre entier." })
  @Min(18, { message: 'Il faut avoir au moins 18 ans.' })
  @Max(120, { message: "L'âge ne peut dépasser 120 ans." })
  age: number;

  @MinLength(6, { message: 'Le mot de passe doit comporter au moins 6 caractères.' })
  motDePasse: string;

   // "confirmation = password" applies to DEUX fields: this is the
   // controller that verifies it
  confirmation: string;
}
  • Line 5: A cleanup function, applied by [@Transform] before validation: a name consisting of spaces is converted to an empty string, and [@IsNotEmpty] rejects it;
  • Lines 18–22: The age is converted to a number and then validated;
  • Lines 27–29: The rule “the confirmation matches the password” applies to two fields: the decorators do not see it, but the controller will verify it.

The file [src/validation.ts]:

import { ClassConstructor, plainToInstance } from 'class-transformer';
import { validate } from 'class-validator';

// errors by field: { name: 'Name is required.', ... }
export type Erreurs = Record<string, string>;

export async function validerFormulaire<T extends object>(
  classe: ClassConstructor<T>,
  corps: Record<string, unknown>,
): Promise<{ dto: T; erreurs: Erreurs }> {
   // 1. received object -> class instance (@Transform / @Type apply)
  const dto = plainToInstance(classe, corps);
   // 2. Check all constraints
  const violations = await validate(dto);
   // 3. Keep the first error message for each field
  const erreurs: Erreurs = {};
  for (const v of violations) {
    erreurs[v.property] = Object.values(v.constraints ?? {})[0];
  }
  return { dto, erreurs };
}
  • line 5: Errors are organized by field: [{ nom: 'Le nom est obligatoire.' }], which allows each message to be displayed under its corresponding field;
  • lines 7–10: the function is generic: it validates any form class. It returns the converted instance ([dto]) and the errors;
  • Lines 17–19: A field can violate multiple constraints; only the first error message is retained.

The case study has the same function ([web/helpers/formulaire.helper.ts]).

The file [src/inscription.controller.ts]:

import { Body, Controller, Get, Post, Query, Render, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Response } from 'express';
import { InscriptionDto } from './inscription.dto';
import { validerFormulaire } from './validation';

@Controller('inscription')
export class InscriptionController {
   // ?html5=1: let the browser validate the form before submission
  @Get()
  @Render('inscription')
  afficher(@Query('html5') html5?: string): object {
    return { valeurs: {}, erreurs: {}, html5: html5 === '1' };
  }

  @Post()
  async inscrire(
    @Body() corps: Record<string, string>,
    @Query('html5') html5: string | undefined,
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): Promise<void> {
    const { dto, erreurs } = await validerFormulaire(InscriptionDto, corps);
     // A rule that applies to two fields
    if (!erreurs.motDePasse && corps.confirmation !== corps.motDePasse) {
      erreurs.confirmation = 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.';
    }
    if (Object.keys(erreurs).length > 0) {
       // RÉAFFICHE the form: entered values (except passwords)
       // and a message below each invalid field
      res.render('inscription', {
        valeurs: { nom: corps.nom, email: corps.email, age: corps.age },
        erreurs,
        erreurGlobale: 'Le formulaire contient des erreurs.',
        html5: html5 === '1',
      });
      return;
    }
    res.render('bienvenue', { nom: dto.nom, email: dto.email, age: dto.age });
  }
}
  • lines 9–13: the empty form. The parameter [html5] will be explained later;
  • line 21: validation of each field;
  • lines 23–25: followed by the rule that applies to two fields;
  • lines 26–36: if there are errors, the form is redisplayed: the entered values (except passwords), errors by field, and a general message;
  • line 37: otherwise, the welcome page, with the values converted by [dto] (age is a number, the name has been cleaned up).
