docs.title: 4.7.1. Validation by the browser
docs.text:
The attributes [required], [maxlength], [min], [max], [type="email"]... instruct the browser to validate the form before submitting it: the user is immediately notified via a tooltip, without any round-trip communication with the server. This is the behavior triggered by the “Enable” link ([/inscription?html5=1]), which removes the [novalidate] attribute from the form.

This validation is a convenience, not a security measure: you can bypass it simply by removing the [required] attribute using the browser’s developer tools, or by sending the request with [curl]. Server-side validation remains essential. That’s why the example disables browser validation by default: to demonstrate how the server works. The case study, however, retains both: the HTML5 attributes for convenience, and server-side validation for security.

docs.title: 4.8. Example 20: The Post/Redirect/Get Pattern
docs.text:
When a POST form submits successfully, the action can display a page directly. The problem arises if the user then refreshes that page (F5 key): the browser resubmits the form, and the operation is performed a second time (an order placed twice, an appointment made twice...). The Post / Redirect / Get pattern (PRG) prevents this problem: a successful POST action does not generate a page; instead, it redirects to a GET page. Reloading this page only sends the GET request, which has no effect.

One detail remains: the GET page must display a message (“the task has been added”), even though this message was generated by the POST action in a different request. It is transmitted in a short-lived cookie, which is read and deleted by the next request: this is a flash message.

The [src/flash.ts] file:

import { NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';

const COOKIE_FLASH = 'flash';

// sets a message that will be displayed by the PROCHAINE page, and only once
export function flash(res: Response, message: string): void {
  res.cookie(COOKIE_FLASH, message, { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax', maxAge: 60_000 });
}

// with each request: any message is passed from the cookie to res.locals (and thus
// to the view template), and the cookie is cleared
export function flashMiddleware(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
  res.locals.flash = req.cookies?.[COOKIE_FLASH] ?? null;
  if (res.locals.flash) {
    res.clearCookie(COOKIE_FLASH);
  }
  next();
}
  • lines 6–8: [res.cookie(nom, valeur, options)] sets a cookie: the browser will send it back with every subsequent request. Options: [httpOnly] (the [JavaScript] from the page cannot read it), [sameSite: 'lax'] (it is not sent by POST requests coming from other sites), [maxAge] (lifetime: one minute, more than enough to track the redirect);
  • Lines 12–18: Middleware executed before each request: any message is passed from the cookie to [res.locals], and thus to the view template, and the cookie is cleared ([res.clearCookie]): the message will be displayed only once.

The file [src/main.ts]:

import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { NestExpressApplication } from '@nestjs/platform-express';
import * as cookieParser from 'cookie-parser';
import { dirname, join } from 'path';
import { AppModule } from './app.module';
import { flashMiddleware } from './flash';

const RACINE = join(__dirname, '..');

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule);
  app.useStaticAssets(join(RACINE, 'public'));
  app.useStaticAssets(join(dirname(require.resolve('bootstrap/package.json')), 'dist'), { prefix: '/bootstrap/' });
  app.setBaseViewsDir(join(RACINE, 'views'));
  app.setViewEngine('hbs');
   // The cookie parser populates req.cookies with the cookies sent by the browser
  app.use(cookieParser());
   // then our middleware reads (and clears) any flash message
  app.use(flashMiddleware);
  await app.listen(3000);
  console.log('Serveur démarré sur http://localhost:3000');
}

bootstrap();
  • line 17: the [cookie-parser] middleware decodes the [Cookie] header from the request and populates the [req.cookies] object;
  • line 19: our middleware, which requires [req.cookies], is registered after it: middleware runs in the order in which it is registered.

The file [src/taches.controller.ts]:

import { Body, Controller, Get, Post, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Response } from 'express';
import { flash } from './flash';
import { TachesService } from './taches.service';

@Controller('taches')
export class TachesController {
  constructor(private readonly taches: TachesService) {}

   // GET /tasks: the list and the add form
  @Get()
  afficher(@Res() res: Response): void {
    res.render('taches', { taches: this.taches.liste() });
  }

   // POST /tasks: the Post/Redirect/Get pattern
  @Post()
  ajouter(@Body('libelle') libelle: string | undefined, @Res() res: Response): void {
    const texte = (libelle ?? '').trim();
    if (texte === '' || texte.length > 40) {
       // Invalid input: the page is reloaded without a redirect
      res.render('taches', {
        taches: this.taches.liste(),
        libelle,
        erreur: 'Le libellé doit comporter de 1 à 40 caractères.',
      });
      return;
    }
    this.taches.ajouter(texte);
    flash(res, `La tâche [${texte}] a été ajoutée.`);
     // No page: redirect to the GET page
    res.redirect('/taches');
  }

   // POST /tasks/no-program: the counterexample (a page in response to POST)
  @Post('sans-prg')
  ajouterSansPrg(@Body('libelle') libelle: string | undefined, @Res() res: Response): void {
    this.taches.ajouter((libelle ?? '').trim() || '(sans titre)');
    res.render('taches', { taches: this.taches.liste(), sansPrg: true });
  }
}
  • lines 11–14: the list page;
  • lines 20–27: an invalid entry: the page is re-displayed (no redirection: the entry and the error message must be retained);
  • lines 29–32: a valid entry: the operation, the pop-up message, then a 302 redirect to the GET page;
  • lines 36–40: the counterexample, for comparison.

docs.title: 4.9. Example 21: Links, Buttons, and Confirmation
docs.text:
A simple rule guides the choice between a link and a button:

  • a link ([<a href>]) generates a GET request. A GET request must not modify anything: browsers, search engines, and antivirus programs may follow links on their own to prepare or analyze a page;
  • an operation that modifies data (add, edit, delete, log out) is a button in a form POST.

Example 21 manages a contact list: you view a contact via a link and delete it using a button, which opens a confirmation window.

The file [src/contacts.controller.ts]:

import { Body, Controller, Get, Param, ParseIntPipe, Post, Render, Res } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Response } from 'express';
import { flash } from './flash';
import { ContactsService } from './contacts.service';

@Controller('contacts')
export class ContactsController {
  constructor(private readonly contacts: ContactsService) {}

   // a LIEN (<a href>): a GET request, which does not modify anything
  @Get()
  @Render('liste')
  liste(): object {
    return { contacts: this.contacts.liste() };
  }

  @Get(':id')
  @Render('fiche')
  fiche(@Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number): object {
    return { contact: this.contacts.lire(id) };
  }

   // a BOUTON in a POST form: a request that modifies data
  @Post(':id')
  enregistrer(
    @Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number,
    @Body() corps: { nom: string; telephone: string },
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): void {
    const contact = this.contacts.modifier(id, corps.nom, corps.telephone);
    flash(res, `Le contact [${contact.nom}] a été modifié.`);
    res.redirect('/contacts');
  }

   // same form, different button (formaction attribute): different action
  @Post(':id/dupliquer')
  dupliquer(
    @Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number,
    @Body() corps: { nom: string; telephone: string },
    @Res() res: Response,
  ): void {
    const copie = this.contacts.ajouter(`${corps.nom} (copie)`, corps.telephone);
    flash(res, `Le contact [${copie.nom}] a été créé.`);
    res.redirect('/contacts');
  }

  @Post(':id/supprimer')
  supprimer(@Param('id', ParseIntPipe) id: number, @Res() res: Response): void {
    const contact = this.contacts.supprimer(id);
    flash(res, `Le contact [${contact.nom}] a été supprimé.`);
    res.redirect('/contacts');
  }
}
  • lines 11–15 and 17–21: the two pages—the list and the contact detail page. [ParseIntPipe] converts the ID; a nonexistent contact results in a 404 error (see the service);
  • lines 24–29: saving a record, using PRG;
  • lines 36–41: duplication, triggered by a second button on the same form (attribute [formaction]);
  • lines 47–52: deletion, via POST.

The file [views/liste.hbs]:

  • lines 12–15: delete: a small form (POST), reduced to its button. The [data-confirmation] attribute contains the question to be asked before submission. The [data-*] attributes are optional: HTML ignores them, while [JavaScript] on the page can read them.

docs.title: 4.9.1. The confirmation window
docs.text:
The browser dialog box ([window.confirm]) cannot be formatted or translated: its buttons remain in the browser’s language. It is replaced by a [Bootstrap] window, written into the page and hidden until needed:

The [views/partials/confirmation.hbs] file:

{{!-- une seule fenêtre pour toute la page, cachée (d-none) au départ --}}
<div id="modale-confirmation" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title">Confirmation</h5>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="modale-confirmation-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="non">Non, revenir</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="oui">Oui, confirmer</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 2: the [d-none] class hides the window;
  • line 3: the gray background;
  • line 11: the question’s position;
  • lines 14–15: the two buttons, identified by the [data-action] attribute.

A bit of [JavaScript] links the forms to the window:

The [public/js/app.js] file:

// Confirmation of forms with the data-confirmation="..." attribute
// Without JavaScript, these forms are simply submitted without confirmation.
(() => {
  const modale = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation');
  const message = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation-message');
  let enAttente = null; // The form to send if confirmation is given

   // 1. We intercept the submission of forms requiring confirmation
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((formulaire) => {
    formulaire.addEventListener('submit', (evenement) => {
      evenement.preventDefault(); // The submission is suspended
      enAttente = formulaire;
      message.textContent = formulaire.dataset.confirmation;
      modale.classList.remove('d-none'); // the window appears
    });
  });

   // 2. The two buttons in the window
  modale.addEventListener('click', (evenement) => {
    const action = evenement.target.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'oui') {
      enAttente.submit(); // Submit, SANS Trigger the 'submit' event again
    } else if (action === 'non') {
      modale.classList.add('d-none');
      enAttente = null;
    }
  });
})();
  • Line 3: The code is wrapped in a function that executes immediately, to avoid creating global variables;
  • lines 9–16: the submission of each form bearing the attribute [data-confirmation] is intercepted. [preventDefault()] suspends the submission; the form is stored, the question is placed in the window ([textContent], not [innerHTML]: the question is displayed as text, never interpreted as HTML), and the window is displayed;
  • Lines 19–27: “Yes” submits the cached form. The [submit()] method of a form submits it without triggering the [submit] event: there is no new confirmation prompt. “No” hides the window.

If [JavaScript] is disabled, the forms simply submit without confirmation: the application still works. This is the principle of incremental improvement: [JavaScript] adds convenience, but it is not essential. The case study follows this principle (its [public/js/app.js] script adds keyboard handling: Esc key, focus). The resulting pages:

Finally, we verify that deletion cannot be triggered by a request for GET:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/contacts/3/delete

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 83

{"message":"Cannot GET /contacts/3/supprimer","error":"Not Found","statusCode":404}
